| `maxAttempts`     | `null`  | Failed attempts before giving up; `null` never gives up                                             |
| `jitter`          | 0.5     | Each wait is drawn uniformly from `(1 − jitter)` to 1 times the nominal wait, here 50 to 100 %      |
| `stableSessionUs` | 10 s    | A session must stay up this long after its hello before its end resets the wait to `initialDelayUs` |

A session that ends sooner than `stableSessionUs` after its hello counts as another failed attempt, so a server that drops every session at once is retried ever more slowly. `ServerConnectionOptions.random` replaces `Math.random` for the jitter in tests. While a retry waits, the card shows `reconnect scheduled`; [Reconnect](/docs/client/server-card#what-each-button-does) skips the wait.

### Timeouts [#timeouts]

`DEFAULT_SERVER_CONNECTION_TIMING`:

| Option                      | Default | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connectDeadlineUs`         | 10 s    | Capability probe, session open and hello exchange. The card shows `connect timeout`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `requestTimeoutUs`          | 10 s    | A request answered by `server.ack` or `server.error`. The card shows `failed (timeout)`.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `snapshotRequestTimeoutUs`  | 10 s    | A `client.snapshot.request`                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `controlWriteTimeoutUs`     | 10 s    | One control-stream write (QUIC flow control). A write still blocked after it fails the session as `transport-error`, so the client reconnects instead of staying "connected" with every request timing out. At most 256 sends wait behind it. |
| `mediaHeaderDeadlineUs`     | 5 s     | How long media stream headers may stay incomplete before the session closes                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `mediaHeaderPollUs`         | 0.25 s  | How often that condition is checked. The check runs only while a header is pending or a channel is held, so an idle session sets no timer for it.                                                                                             |
| `sessionCloseGraceUs`       | 0.25 s  | After a fatal transport error, how long to wait for the session’s own close                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ownPlacementResultGraceUs` | 5 s     | After an accepted placement commit, how long a placement update counts as this client’s own result (interim, see [Contract gaps](/docs/client/developer/interim-behaviour))                                                                   |

`validateTiming` rejects zero or negative timeouts, a `maxDelayUs` below `initialDelayUs`, and a `jitter` outside 0 to 1.

## Fixed timing [#fixed-timing]

These are constants, not options:

| Constant                        | Value | File                                     | Meaning                                                     |
| ------------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LOCK_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_US`    | 5 s   | `client/src/state/setupLock.ts`          | The lock holder renews the setup lock this often            |
| `LOCK_EXPIRY_US`                | 15 s  | `client/src/state/setupLock.ts`          | A lock runs out this long after its last renewal            |
| `PING_INTERVAL_US`              | 10 s  | `client/src/connections/clockSync.ts`    | Clock-sync ping interval, for the card’s `min RTT`          |
| `PING_TIMEOUT_US`               | 5 s   | `client/src/connections/clockSync.ts`    | A pong later than this is ignored                           |
| `PROGRESS_ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL_MS` | 5 s   | `client/src/calibration/announcement.ts` | Screen readers hear calibration progress at most this often |


# Contract gaps and interim behaviour (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/interim-behaviour)



Some behaviour on the user pages depends on questions the protocol contract (`protocol/wire-format.md`) hasn’t settled yet. The client picks one reading in the meantime, marked `INTERIM` in the code, and the mock server follows the client’s proposal. A real server may behave differently until the arbiter decides. This page lists each gap that users can notice, with its change request in `protocol/changes/`, and the requests the arbiter has since decided.

## Gaps users can notice [#gaps-users-can-notice]

| Topic                                          | Change request (status on 2026-10-18)                        | What the client does now                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | What the user pages say                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Network calibration                            | 0018                                                         | No network calibration stream; the setup view’s Network section shows `Network calibration is not available yet.` The card’s budget line shows whatever budget the server sends. An incoming stream whose first frame is not a media header is cancelled (code 0) with a warning in the client’s per-server connection log; the session continues.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | “Network calibration isn’t available yet.”                                                                                                                                      |
| Camera-pose calibration screen                 | Not defined by the contract yet                              | The Camera pose section is exactly a red, bold, italic `TODO`, with no controls: darker red on the light theme, lighter red on the dark one, so it meets WCAG AA contrast on both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | “Camera-pose calibration isn’t available in the client yet.”                                                                                                                    |
| Placement commit with an expected revision     | Contract names `expectedRevision` but not the server’s check | Sends the draft’s base revision and blocks a stale commit locally. The mock server accepts only while its placement is still at that revision, and otherwise rejects with `stale-revision`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [Place a server in the scene](/docs/client/placement-editing): “A server should accept the commit only while its placement is still at that revision, as the mock server does.” |
| Revision steps                                 | 0007, accepted 2026-10-17                                    | Enforced: every authoritative update, stream descriptors and calibration results included, must step `metadataRevision` by exactly +1 (§10). A gap or a duplicate (or a step backwards, or an update that breaks a rule, such as a placement that isn’t rigid) triggers one snapshot resync and keeps the session. Messages that don’t step the revision (operator state, replay-complete, the network budget at the current revision) are not counted. A placement commit is two steps: the payload (or its substitute notice) at N+1, then `revision-changed` at N+2. A descriptor’s revision below the snapshot’s is accepted (§6). | The card’s `resynchronising` line.                                                                                                                                              |
| Media stream lifecycle                         | 0009                                                         | Media before `client.subscribe` is accepted for held bundles; subscriptions last one session and aren’t re-sent after a reconnect.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Not visible beyond the card’s counts.                                                                                                                                           |
| Protocol 1.1: §1a HTTP answers and close codes | 0024, accepted 2026-10-11                                    | The client does not map the close codes 0–5 to its own states yet, and the mock simulates none of the 421/404/403/503 answers. A close is reported as `remote` with its code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Not visible beyond the card's close reason.                                                                                                                                     |

## Decided by the arbiter (protocol #383, 2026-10-17) [#decided-by-the-arbiter-protocol-383-2026-10-17]

These were gaps on this page. The client now follows the contract, except where a row names what remains.

| Topic                                            | Change request                    | What the client does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | User page                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Empty media streams and the end-of-stream record | 0004, accepted                    | A stream finished before its header is `frame-truncated`. A record has `endOfStream` set exactly when its payload is empty, and then no other flag; anything else is `invalid-message` and fails that server’s session.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Not visible beyond the card’s close reason.                                                                                |
| Integers in control JSON                         | 0005, accepted                    | Every integer in a control message has magnitude at most 2^53−1; microsecond fields are in \[0, 2^53−1]. A larger value is `invalid-message`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Not visible.                                                                                                               |
| Replies, `replyTo` and the lock expiry           | 0008, accepted                    | Each request gets exactly one reply, after the broadcasts it causes. With a minor-1 server the client recognises its own calibration result and placement update by `replyTo`; without it, by its pending request. A refresh for cameras, bundles or quantization asks with `revision-refresh` (minor-1 servers only). Another client’s lock expiry is still the one the server last announced: the server re-announces it when a renewal moves it by at least 1 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | [Read a server card](/docs/client/server-card#details): `expiry passed as last announced; the server may have renewed it`. |
| HEVC payload format                              | 0010, accepted                    | Annex-B access units with VPS, SPS and PPS in every keyframe record; no `hvcC`; the decoder is configured from `codecString` alone. Each codec-config record’s SPS is checked against the channel’s `codecString`, which must be the `hev1` form of the SPS `profile_tier_level` (trailing zero constraint bytes omitted, §6). On a mismatch, or with no SPS, that channel’s decoder is not configured, the bundle is undecodable and the log names the reason (`level`, `profile`, `tier`, `constraint-bytes`, `hvc1`, `no-sps`, …). Vectors: `protocol/vectors/codec-string/`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | A live server’s card shows **decoder failed** for that bundle.                                                             |
| Coordinate frame and pixel centre                | 0011 option A, accepted           | Metres, **left-handed**, +X right, +Y up, +Z forward (§9). A depth pixel’s centre is at its integer coordinate, v down: `pointDepthCamera = ((u − cx)·z/fx, −(v − cy)·z/fy, z)`. Tile-view overlays (`tileToCss`) use the same pixel convention.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | [Move around the 3D view](/docs/client/viewer): a mirrored cloud is a server or recording that does not convert its poses. |
| Wire poses                                       | 0022, accepted                    | The server sends camera poses already in the §9 frame (C·M·C, C = diag(1, −1, 1, 1)); the client applies them as they are. The `geometry-*` conformance vectors pin the result with a non-identity pose.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Same row as above.                                                                                                         |
| Meaning of a calibration result                  | 0012 superseded by 0023, accepted | A solved run stays `running` and waits for Commit; with a minor-1 server its `awaitingCommit` says so, otherwise the message (`… awaiting commit`). `server.calibration.result` is sent only on a commit (in force at once) or a failure. Cancel, leave, lock loss and disconnect abandon the run: nothing is committed and no result is sent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | [Calibrate depth](/docs/client/calibration) and [Set up a server](/docs/client/setup-workspace).                           |
| Recording manifest                               | 0038, accepted                    | Reads a recording folder with `manifest.json` version 1 (Appendix B; schema `protocol/schema/recording-manifest.json`): relative file paths, per-bundle segments, in-progress trimming, cameras sent on one timeline by frame set index, and handed to the 3D view together only at equal index (B.5). Two client departures from B.5 remain: a frame set waits at most 100 ms for every camera that has a frame there (`src/media/playback/frameSetHold.ts`; B.5 sets no bound), then hands over the cameras it has; and the hold aligns the hand-off to the renderer, not the frame drawn, so after a timeout the missing camera’s previous frame stays visible next to the newer ones. A newer complete frame set drops older waiting ones, and a frame of an index already handed over is late and dropped; both count as dropped on the card. A manifest without `manifestVersion` (the pre-0038 format) is refused, as B.2 requires, with a message that names `scripts/convert-manifest.mjs`. | [Play a recording](/docs/client/playback).                                                                                 |

Error codes such as `not-lock-owner`, `calibration-running`, `calibration-not-running` and `stale-revision` are the mock server’s own. The contract doesn’t fix server error codes for these cases, so the user pages quote them only as the mock server’s. Protocol 1.1 names `lock-held`, `invalid-lease`, `role-required` and `rate-limited` (§11).

## Protocol references still on screen [#protocol-references-still-on-screen]

None. The UI strings in `client/src/ui/` carry no change-request numbers or § references. The last two messages that cited the contract now say the rule in plain words (2026-09-28):

* `Not applied: The pose must be rigid: scale, shear, mirroring and perspective are not allowed.` comes from `client/src/calibration/placementDraft.ts` (§9 requires placements to be rigid transforms). The placement fields and handle can’t produce such a pose.
* `depth bitstream has 8-bit luma; depth must be 10-bit` comes from `client/src/media/playback/recordingManifest.ts` (§8 defines depth as one 10-bit code per pixel).

## Keep this page current [#keep-this-page-current]

When the arbiter accepts or changes one of these requests, move its row to the decided table and update the matching user page in the same PR. The client’s full list of interim decisions is in `client/docs/development/ROADMAP.md`, and the mock server’s is at the top of `client/src/media/playback/mockServer.ts`.


# Latency measurement (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/latency)



The client has three tools for measuring its own latency:

* **The per-stage latency probe** (`client/src/connections/latencyProbe.ts`). It times each frame through the client, from the last network byte to the animation frame after the draw, and reports p50/p90/p99/max per stage. It is off unless a pipeline asks for it. When off, no clock is read on the media path.
* **The latency check page** (`client/dev/latency-check.html`). It runs the probe in a real browser over two recordings and shows the stage table.
* **The end-to-end benchmark** (`npm run bench:e2e`). It runs the client media path in Node with the browser parts simulated, and can compare two commits.

The main app does not turn the probe on. Only the latency check page and your own code do.

## Latency stages [#latency-stages]

All values are in milliseconds.

| Stage              | Channel       | From → to                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `network`          | colour, depth | capture (server clock, converted with the clock-sync offset) → last byte of the record read by the client  |
| `transport`        | colour, depth | last byte read → record handed to its decoder (framing, router, keyframe gate)                             |
| `queue`            | colour, depth | record handed to the decoder → `decode()` returned                                                         |
| `decode`           | colour, depth | `decode()` returned → decoded frame output                                                                 |
| `pairWait`         | colour, depth | frame decoded → colour/depth pair emitted (waiting for the other channel)                                  |
| `depthRead`        | pair          | pair emitted → depth codes read into the upload buffer                                                     |
| `upload`           | pair          | depth codes read → depth and colour uploads issued                                                         |
| `draw`             | pair          | uploads issued → next render-loop tick that drew                                                           |
| `present`          | pair          | that draw → the next render-loop tick; an upper bound for the hand-off to the compositor, not the scan-out |
| `clientTotal`      | pair          | last byte of the later channel → `present`                                                                 |
| `captureToPresent` | pair          | capture → `present`                                                                                        |

A stage is left out of the report until it has a sample. For example, `network` has no samples until the clock-sync offset is known. The window is the last 512 samples per stage and channel.

## Run the latency check page [#run-the-latency-check-page]

You need `client/reference/hevc-web/` with `gpu-output-color.hevc`, `gpu-output-depth.hevc` and, optionally, `public/hevcsetup.json`.

These sample recordings aren’t published and aren’t in the repository, so this page can only run where a local copy exists. See [Sample recordings](/docs/client/developer/test-the-client#sample-recordings).

Start the dev server in `client/`:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open this URL in Chrome:

```text
http://localhost:5173/dev/latency-check.html?autorun=1&engine=webgl2
```

URL parameters:

| Parameter                          | Effect                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `autorun=1`                        | Start on load. Without it, press **Start**.                                             |
| `engine=webgl2` or `engine=webgpu` | Force a rendering engine. Without it, WebGPU is tried first and WebGL2 is the fallback. |
| `seconds=N`                        | Measuring time after the first upload, default 8, maximum 60.                           |

What the page does:

* It plays both recordings through the real connection, decoding, pairing, feed and renderer code. It uses a **synthetic decoder** that ignores the HEVC bytes and emits generated frames.
* It waits for both servers to upload a pair (at most 30 s), then discards 1 s of start-up samples, then measures for `seconds`.

### Cross-origin isolation [#cross-origin-isolation]

The dev server sends `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. This makes the page cross-origin isolated, so `performance.now()` keeps a 5 µs resolution in Chrome instead of 100 µs. Some client stages, such as `transport` and `queue`, take tens of µs or less, so they need the fine timer. `vite preview` and the production build do not send these headers.

## What you should see [#what-you-should-see]

When the run ends, `document.body.dataset.state` is `done` or `failed`. The HUD shows:

* a status line: state, engine, `crossOriginIsolated`, measured timer resolution;
* one stage table per server, with `n`, p50, p90, p99 and max in ms.

The full report is under **report JSON** at the bottom right, and in `window.__latencyCheckReport`. It contains:

* `crossOriginIsolated` and `timerResolutionMs`;
* `entries[].latency.stages[]`, where each stage has `stage`, `channel`, `count`, `p50`, `p90`, `p99` and `max`;
* `errors`, `notes` and `verdict`.

`done` means every server uploaded pairs, there were no errors, and every server has `present` samples. The recorded run is in `client/docs/development/latency-audit.md` §9.2: headless Chromium, WebGL2 on SwiftShader, `seconds=8`, timer resolution 0.005 ms. Its p50 values:

| Stage       | p50              |
| ----------- | ---------------- |
| `transport` | 0.015 ms         |
| `queue`     | 0.005 ms or less |
| `depthRead` | 0.10 ms          |
| `upload`    | 3.17 ms          |
| `draw`      | 30.5 ms          |
| `present`   | 67.7 ms          |

### Which stages mean something on this page [#which-stages-mean-something-on-this-page]

| Stage                             | Meaningful here?                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `transport`, `queue`, `depthRead` | Yes. Production code.                                                                                               |
| `upload`                          | Yes, for the engine in use. On SwiftShader it is software rendering.                                                |
| `decode`                          | No. It times the synthetic decoder, not WebCodecs.                                                                  |
| `pairWait`                        | Partly. The synthetic decoder outputs colour about 15 ms before depth, so colour `pairWait` shows that skew.        |
| `network`, `captureToPresent`     | No. Recordings have no network, and the capture time comes from the recording’s clock.                              |
| `draw`, `present`, `clientTotal`  | Only on a real GPU. On SwiftShader the points are rasterised on the CPU, so render-loop ticks are tens of ms apart. |

To measure real decode, network and display time, use a real server and a real browser decoder. The probe measures the same stages there.

### Use the probe in your own code [#use-the-probe-in-your-own-code]

Set `latencyProbe: true` in the `ConnectionManager` options, or in the options of `startAppRuntime` for a whole runtime (ignored with `media: 'none'`). The manager passes it to every `ServerPipeline`. Then read the report:

```ts
// `options`: your usual ConnectionManager options.
const manager = new ConnectionManager({ ...options, latencyProbe: true });
const id = manager.add(source);
// Later, for example once per second:
const report = manager.pipeline(id)?.latencyReport(); // null when the probe is off
manager.pipeline(id)?.resetLatency(); // clear the windows
```

`latencyReport()` sorts the sample windows, so call it for diagnostics, not per frame.

## Run the end-to-end benchmark [#run-the-end-to-end-benchmark]

This runs the client media path in Node. The path is: byte source, transport, router, keyframe gate, decoder, pairing, feed, then a recording upload target. The browser parts are simulated:

* `EncodedVideoChunk` copies its data unless given a transfer list;
* decode takes 0 ms;
* `VideoFrame.copyTo` is a memcpy;
* on stream rotation and reconnect, the support probe takes 1 ms and a new decoder’s first output takes 10 ms.

The numbers are therefore client overhead in Node, not browser timings.

In `client/`:

```bash
npm run bench:e2e
```

To use BYOB reads on the media streams:

```bash
npm run bench:e2e -- --byob
```

It takes about 20 s and prints three blocks:

* `steady 640x576`;
* `steady 1920x576`;
* a rotation line.

Each steady block shows:

* per-stage µs p50 / p99;
* `client-added total` (last byte of the pair → uploads issued);
* JS-visible copies per frame set;
* `exact-code failures`, which must be 0.

Results on the current code, 2026-09-28:

| Line                    | 640×576      | 1920×576     |
| ----------------------- | ------------ | ------------ |
| client-added total, p50 | about 0.5 ms | about 0.8 ms |
| copies per frame set    | 19.3 KiB     | 61.5 KiB     |

* With `--byob`, copies are 0.0 KiB.
* The rotation line shows a first upload about 1.2 ms after a new stream, and about 12 ms after a reconnect. It shows 2 `isConfigSupported` calls.
* Absolute times depend on the machine.

### Compare against another commit [#compare-against-another-commit]

From the repository root, replacing `43ad3cd` with the commit to compare:

```bash
git worktree add --detach ../bench-before 43ad3cd
ln -s "$PWD/client/node_modules" ../bench-before/client/node_modules
(cd client && npm run bench:e2e -- --root ../../bench-before/client)
git worktree remove ../bench-before
```

The output labels each block with the other tree’s path. Against `43ad3cd`, on the same machine as the results above:

|                         | 640×576      | 1920×576     |
| ----------------------- | ------------ | ------------ |
| client-added total, p50 | about 3.1 ms | about 9.1 ms |

The rotation line showed about 20 ms and 24 `isConfigSupported` calls.

The other tree must have the same module layout (`src/connections/transport.ts`, `src/media/decoding/decodingSink.ts`, `src/rendering/renderFeed.ts`, and so on). See `client/scripts/bench/README.md`.

## Fix measurement problems [#fix-measurement-problems]

### `crossOriginIsolated` is false, or `timerResolutionMs` is 0.1 [#crossoriginisolated-is-false-or-timerresolutionms-is-01]

* The page was not served by the Vite dev server with its headers.
* Open it through `npm run dev` at `http://localhost:5173`.
* Check the headers:

  ```bash
  curl -sI http://localhost:5173/dev/latency-check.html | grep -i cross-origin
  ```

  Both `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy` must appear. Sub-millisecond stages are unreliable without them.

### `failed` with “no pair uploaded by every server within the timeout” after 30 s [#failed-with-no-pair-uploaded-by-every-server-within-the-timeout-after-30-s]

* The recordings are probably missing from `client/reference/hevc-web/`.
* The dev server answers a missing file with its HTML index page (HTTP 200), so the page does not fail at the download. It fails 30 s later because nothing can be played.
* Without the unpublished sample recordings, this check can’t pass.

### `failed` with “rendering-incompatible: WebGPU required but unavailable” [#failed-with-rendering-incompatible-webgpu-required-but-unavailable]

* `engine=webgpu` was forced in a browser without a WebGPU adapter, for example headless Chromium without a GPU.
* Use `engine=webgl2`, or run in a headed Chrome on a machine with a supported GPU.

### `failed` with “VideoFrame (WebCodecs) unavailable (secure context required)” [#failed-with-videoframe-webcodecs-unavailable-secure-context-required]

* The page was opened over plain HTTP from another machine.
* Use `localhost`, or serve with HTTPS.

### `draw` and `present` are tens of milliseconds [#draw-and-present-are-tens-of-milliseconds]

* The render loop ticks that slowly because the renderer is software (SwiftShader, typical in headless Chromium).
* These two stages are only meaningful on a real GPU.

### `--root` fails with “Cannot find module” [#--root-fails-with-cannot-find-module]

* The other tree has no `node_modules`. Create the symlink shown in the procedure.
* Or the other tree’s module layout is too old for the harness.

## Other dev check pages [#other-dev-check-pages]

The decode, render and wiring checks are described on [Test the client](/docs/client/developer/test-the-client#open-the-dev-check-pages).


# Mock server (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/mock-server)



The mock server (`client/src/media/playback/mockServer.ts`) simulates one OrbbecStreamer capture server inside the client, on the same byte-level seam a WebTransport session uses. Real `ServerConnection`s connect to it, so the following run exactly as against a real server, with no network and no hardware:

* the handshake and snapshots;
* the setup lock, calibration and placement commits;
* shared-update filtering;
* media streams.

How it behaves:

* **Sessions**: one `MockServer` holds one server state. Every client that opens it gets its own session, and a reconnect opens a new session.
* **Time**: it comes only from the scheduler you pass in. With a `ManualScheduler`, every run is deterministic.
* **Media**: it comes from a recording (`.hevc` colour and depth files plus a manifest), the same format as recording playback. Without a recording the server has no media.
* **Contract readings**: the mock follows the contract, including the 2026-10-17 rulings (replies and `replyTo` §3b, change 0008; calibration results and `awaitingCommit` §11, change 0023; revision steps §10, change 0007). Where the contract is still open (change 0014) it follows the client’s proposal, listed at the top of `mockServer.ts` and on [Contract gaps and interim behaviour](/docs/client/developer/interim-behaviour).

## Use the mock server [#use-the-mock-server]

In a test:

```ts
const scheduler = new ManualScheduler(0n);
const created = createMockServer({ scheduler, snapshot: snapshotFixture() });
if (!created.ok) throw new Error(created.issues.join('; '));
const mock = created.value;
const connection = new ServerConnection({
  url: mock.url,
  opener: mock.opener(), // one opener per client
  scheduler,
  // clientId, displayName, platform, decoderProbe, ...
});
await connection.connect();
```

With media, create it from a recording:

```ts
const created = createMockServerFromRecording(manifest, bytesByKey, scheduler);
```

In a dev page or in composition code, add it as a source:

```ts
manager.add({ kind: 'mock', server: mock });
```

Create the mock on the same scheduler as the connection manager. Each connection manager that uses the same mock is another client of the same server. Two entries in one manager reach the same server id, and the second one reports a conflict.

Useful controls:

* **Scenario**: `setStreaming`, `setBundleAvailability`, and calibration scripts passed in `createMockServer({ calibration })`: duration, progress interval, accepted or failed, new camera poses or a new depth profile, and a depth-code histogram per progress message (`depthHistogram`; `syntheticDepthHistogram` in `src/dev/devMock.ts` is a ready-made one). The shell’s “Add mock server” scripts a 6 s depth-quantization run with that histogram.
* **Camera-pose data** (change 0033): a camera-pose run sends `server.calibration.progress` at run start, then at most 10 times a second, with `phase`, `lastSolveFailure`, `sharedObservations` and per camera the corners, accepted count, last observation and an 8 x 6 coverage grid; the camera-pose calibration entry carries `board`, `timeoutMs` and `maxReprojectionErrorPx` (`createMockServer({ cameraPose: { statusFields: false } })` omits them; `timeoutMs` sets the limit). Script it with `calibration['camera-pose'].pose`: `blindCameras` (never see the board), `isolatedCameras` (rejected `not-co-observed`, in no pair), `rejectReasons` (per camera, any kebab-case reason), `solveFailure` (keeps the run in `solving` with that `lastSolveFailure`), `neverSolves`, `minPairCountForRms`. A run that never solves ends at `timeoutMs`: result `accepted: false`, state `failed` (a valid pose stays `valid` with the message). A one-camera snapshot has no shared pairs. Cancel, lease loss, takeover and capture stop restore the pre-run record and stop progress; sensor and profile writes are refused `calibration-running` while a run exists.
* **Refused connects** (§1a, change 0024): `createMockServer({ connectRefusal })` or `mock.refuseConnects(refusal | null)`. `{ kind: 'status', status: 421 | 404 | 403 | 503 | 400 }` and `{ kind: 'quic-busy' }` reject the opener at once with a browser-like `WebTransportError` that carries no status, as Chromium does; `{ kind: 'no-answer' }` never answers, so the client's connect deadline fires. `mock.refusedConnects` lists the answers given. Close codes after the hello: `closeSession(session, code, reason)`.
* **Near-range depth**: `nearRangeQuantizationProfile()` (`src/media/playback/nearRangeProfile.ts`, 200 to 5000 mm, from a live server profile) as the snapshot's `quantization`. In the dev app, `?mockDepth=near` makes **Add mock server** serve it (snapshot only, no media).
* **Role**: the dev mock grants `operator` (`roleGrant`), as a server does for a page opened on the server machine. `?mockRole=viewer` makes **Add mock server** grant `viewer`: setup and placement are then disabled with "needs the operator role (open on the server machine)" (change 0048).
* **Floor** (change 0046): `?mockFloor=1` makes **Add mock server** offer the feature `floor`. The mock then has a `floor` item (`missing` at first) and a scripted floor run under the lease: progress with a candidate plane (normal about (0.02, 0.999, -0.03), 1.35 m), then awaiting commit; **Commit** raises the floor revision and sets `poseRevision` to the camera-pose revision; **Cancel** restores the item. A camera-pose commit makes the floor `stale`. `?mockFloor=fail` ends the run with `no-plane: ...` instead. In tests use `floor: true` or `floor: { plane, quality, durationUs, progressIntervalUs, failure }`. A session that did not list `floor` never sees the item, and `kind: 'floor'` from it closes the session as `invalid-message`.
* **Calibration quality** (change 0045): `?mockQuality=1` makes **Add mock server** offer the feature `calibration-quality`. Every calibration item then carries `advisories`, the camera-pose item carries `poseQuality`, camera-pose progress carries the last solve attempt and camera-pose results carry `quality`, all deterministic (3 cameras: `cam-a`, `cam-b`, `cam-c`). `?mockQuality=advisory` adds advisories whose figures agree with them (`reprojection-above-target`, `depth-bias-high`, `alignment-uses-factory-intrinsics`, `depth-range-clipped` on the depth record, and an unknown future code on the floor once one is committed). Figures are only for the cameras in the snapshot, so the one-camera dev mock has no pairs and no pair advisory; in tests `MOCK_QUALITY_PAIR_SCENARIO` adds `pair-consistency-above-target` with the first pair at 14.2 mm (needs at least two cameras). Attempt figures appear only in `solving` progress. `?mockQuality=legacy` starts the records without reports (`quality-unknown`, no `poseQuality`) until a commit writes one. The mock serves `client.calibration.report.get` to operator sessions, with the three report formats, `report: null` when a kind has no report, and the pre-run report during a run; a viewer gets `role-required`. In tests use `calibrationQuality: true` or `{ advisories: { 'camera-pose': [...], 'depth-quantization': [...], floor: [...] }, rmsPx, legacyCommitted }`. A session that did not list the feature sees none of it, and its `client.calibration.report.get` ends the session as `unknown-message-type`. See [calibration quality API](/docs/client/developer/calibration-quality).
* **Faults**: `dropSession`, `closeSession`, `delaySession`, `stallSession` / `resumeSession`, `sendMalformed`, `skipRevisions`, `sendStaleRevision`, `refuseSnapshots`, `expireLease`, `holdLocalConsoleLease`, `session.dropFromNetwork()`.
* **Inspection**: `sessions()`, `sessionOf(clientId)`, `lockHolder()`, `snapshot()`, `metadataRevision`, `getRequestLog()`, `session.requestCounts`, `session.role`, `session.mediaStats(bundleId)`.

## Fake protocol 1.1: roles, takeover, lease cap, rate limits [#fake-protocol-11-roles-takeover-lease-cap-rate-limits]

The mock follows wire-format §11 and §16 of protocol 1.1. Pass these to `createMockServer`:

| Option                   | Default      | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `roleGrant`              | `'viewer'`   | `'operator'`: a session whose hello asks for `operator` gets it. `'by-hello'`: it gets it only when its peer is loopback and its origin equals `consoleOrigin`. A session that doesn't ask, or announces 1.0, is always a viewer. |
| `consoleOrigins`         | none         | The list of origins `'by-hello'` compares with, for example `['https://localhost:8443']`: the server's configured console origins. Any listed origin is granted.                                                                  |
| `consoleOrigin`          | none         | One origin; the single-value form of `consoleOrigins`. Both together are combined.                                                                                                                                                |
| `serverMinor`            | `1`          | `0` runs a 1.0 server: no `role` in the hello, `takeover` ignored.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `strictMinor0Hello`      | `false`      | Rejects a hello with any field a 1.0 hello doesn't have, as a 1.0 server does: `server.error{fatal: true, code: 'invalid-message'}`, then close code 1. Use it with `serverMinor: 0` to test the client's one retry.              |
| `rateLimit`              | 10, then 2/s | One budget per session for acquire, placement commit and calibration start and commit. Over it, the ack is `rate-limited` and nothing changes. `false` turns it off.                                                              |
| `leaseMaxLifetimeUs`     | 30 min       | The lease cap. At the cap the lease ends as on expiry, and only that session gets `rate-limited` for 15 s.                                                                                                                        |
| `helloDeadlineUs`        | off          | Closes a session without a hello: `hello-timeout`, then close code 3.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `legacyLeaseInvalidCode` | `false`      | Answers a wrong lease with the old `lease-invalid` instead of `invalid-lease`.                                                                                                                                                    |

## Fake capture idle mode (protocol 1.1) [#fake-capture-idle-mode-protocol-11]

A real server keeps its cameras closed until a client asks it to open them (wire-format §10, §11, §18; change 0039). The mock fakes that with the `capture` option:

```ts
createMockServer({
  snapshot,                       // the rig's content while the cameras are open
  capture: { initial: 'idle', openDurationUs: 2_000_000n, closeDurationUs: 500_000n },
  scheduler,
});
```

| Option                    | Default                         | Effect                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `capture.initial`         | `'running'`                     | `'idle'`: the server starts with its cameras closed. The snapshot has `capture.state: 'idle'`, empty `cameras`, `bundles` and `bundleAvailability`, and streaming `stopped`. |
| `capture.openDurationUs`  | 2 s                             | How long `opening` lasts before `running` (or `failed`).                                                                                                                     |
| `capture.closeDurationUs` | 500 ms                          | How long `closing` lasts before `idle`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `capture.devices`         | one connected device per camera | `capture.devices` while the cameras are closed. `null`: the server cannot enumerate.                                                                                         |
| `capture.openFailure`     | none                            | Every open fails with this text.                                                                                                                                             |

Controls: `captureState()`, `setCaptureOpenFailure(message | null)`, `setCaptureDevices(devices)` (hot-plug) and `failCapture(message)` (a running rig fails).

What the mock does, message for message as §18 says:

* **Start** (`client.capture.start`, no lease, no role): refused `lock-held` while another session holds the lock. Running: acknowledged at once. Idle or failed: `opening`, then after the open one atomic commit: `server.capture.state{running}`, `server.metadata.revision-changed` for `cameras` and `bundles`, a `server.stream.descriptor` per channel, `server.streaming`, and only then each pending start's ack. A failed open sends `server.capture.state{failed}` and then `capture-start-failed` with the same text. A start during `closing` is queued and reopens after `idle`.
* **Stop** (`client.capture.stop`): needs the `operator` role (`role-required`), then the lease (`invalid-lease`). It finishes every media stream, abandons a calibration run without a result, publishes `closing`, the revision notice (invalidating streams) and `streaming{stopped, capture-not-running}`, then `idle`, and acknowledges. A stop while opening aborts the open and answers pending starts `capture-stopped`.
* **Calibration start** while the cameras are not running is refused `capture-not-running`, before its other rules.
* **1.0 sessions**: never get `capture` or `server.capture.state`. While the cameras are not running, their hello is answered with a fatal `server.error{capture-not-running}`; when the cameras close, they are closed with the same error before the revision notice.

On the client, `connection.startCapture()` and `connection.stopCapture()` (also on the pipeline) wait up to 60 s for the deferred ack. `startCapture()` while one is pending fails `already-pending` without sending, and both fail `unsupported-by-server` below protocol 1.1. `state.capture` is `null` for a server that does not report it (1.0), and the card label follows it before the lock and readiness.

## Fake the operator state (protocol 1.1) [#fake-the-operator-state-protocol-11]

Changes 0027 to 0033 add operator-only messages (sensors, stream profiles, sync telemetry), the task list every session gets, and preview media. The mock fakes them with the `operatorState` option. Every part is off unless you name it, so an operator session still gets only `server.operator.replay-complete` by default.

```ts
createMockServer({
  snapshot,
  roleGrant: 'operator',
  operatorState: { sensors: true, profiles: true, telemetry: true, setupProgress: true, preview: true },
  scheduler,
});
```

| Option          | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sensors`       | A Femto Bolt registry per camera: colour auto-exposure, exposure 1..300 (inert while auto-exposure is on), gain, white balance, brightness, power line as an enum, a `requiresRestart` property (`backlight-compensation`); depth noise removal with two dependents and a read-only exposure 20..125. `{ deviceClamp, restartDurationUs }`: a clamp the device applies inside the advertised range, and how long a restart takes (default 3 s). |
| `profiles`      | Four profiles: two compatible at 30 and 15 fps, one that needs an engine build and invalidates calibration, one incompatible. `{ list, active, switchDurationUs }` replaces them (default 2 s per switch or revert).                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `telemetry`     | One `server.sync.telemetry` window per second while capture runs. `{ intervalUs, toleranceUs, captureFps, decimated }`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `setupProgress` | `engine-build`, `camera-open` and `encoder-start` to every minor-1 session. The last two mirror `capture`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `preview`       | Descriptors carry `preview: true` while `needs-setup` (or a camera-pose run started while ready). Media and `available: true` go to operator sessions whose hello has `"preview-media"`; everyone else gets `available: false, reason: 'needs-setup'`.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `coalesceGate`  | Default true: a coalescable message is held while 64 KiB or more is unsent (§12 item 5).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

What the mock does:

* **Delivery.** Operator-only messages go to `operator` sessions only. The replay after every hello and snapshot is in the §12 order with `replyTo: null`: per camera its capabilities and one config per sensor, the profiles, the latest telemetry, the task list, then the marker. A session that is not an operator gets only the task list, with no marker. While `capture` is not running there are no cameras, so no capabilities, config or telemetry.
* **Sensor writes.** Role, then lease, then capture, then `calibration-running`, `sensor-busy`, the camera, and the whole request is validated before anything is applied (known, writable, type, range, step grid, `enabledWhen` in order). The originator's `server.sensor.config` copy carries `replyTo` and comes before the ack; a request that changes nothing gets only the ack. A `requiresRestart` property is acknowledged at the start, sends `streaming: starting`, and is `sensor-busy` for every camera until it ends.
* **Profile switches.** Role, lease, capture, `calibration-running`, `profile-switch-in-progress`, `profile-unknown`, `profile-incompatible`. A real switch sends `switching`, the ack, the pause, `streaming: starting`, then after `switchDurationUs` one commit: the revision notice (invalidating streams), descriptors, and `idle` with `replyTo` for the originator. A profile with `invalidatesCalibration` makes those calibrations `stale`, so the server returns to `needs-setup`.
* **Coalescing.** Config, profiles, telemetry and task-list messages keep at most one unsent copy per key per session, latest wins, stamped when written. Config is sent at most once a second per camera and sensor, progress at most four times a second; a copy with `replyTo`, and any change of a task's state, is never held back. A stalled session shows it: `session.queuedCoalescableKeys`.

Controls:

* `narrowSensorRange(cameraId, sensor, propertyId, { min, max })`: the capabilities are sent again.
* `failNextSensorApply('ack' | 'after-ack' | null)`: the device fails the second change (the ack is `sensor-apply-failed`), or fails a restart after its ack (`server.error{replyTo: null}`).
* `setCameraConnected(cameraId, connected)`: one `cameras` revision change and new capabilities.
* `failNextProfileSwitch('revert' | 'revert-fails' | null)`: the device refuses the profile and the mock reverts (`reverting`, then `idle` on the old profile, then `server.error{profile-apply-failed}`), or the revert fails too and capture ends `failed`.
* `setTelemetryFault({ kind: 'degraded' | 'lost' | 'no-signal' | 'signal-unreportable', cameraId } | null)`, `silenceTelemetry(durationUs)`, `telemetryWindow()`.
* `setSetupTask(taskId, patch)`, `restartSetupProgress()`, `setupTasks()`: script `engine-build` (progress, `failed` with an `error`, `done` back to `running`) or simulate a server restart.

Busy codes (operator ruling 2026-10-12, going into wire-format): a `profile.set` while a switch is pending, even for the pending or active profile, is `profile-switch-in-progress`; a `profile.set` during a sensor restart, and a sensor write during a profile switch, are `sensor-busy`. Entering or leaving preview is its own revision notice even when it coincides with a calibration commit.

Open a session with transport facts for the grant rule with `mock.opener({ loopback: true, origin: 'https://localhost:8443' })`. The default peer is not loopback and has no origin.

A takeover (`client.lock.acquire{takeover: true}` from an operator session) ends the current lease as on expiry. It abandons a running calibration without any `server.calibration.result`, restores the calibration state, and broadcasts one `server.lock.state` with the new owner. `mock.holdLocalConsoleLease()` does the same for the server's own console (owner `local-console`, name `local operator console`), whose lease needs no heartbeat. `releaseLocalConsoleLease()` ends it.

Operator sessions get `server.operator.replay-complete` after every hello and snapshot. A heartbeat that would move the expiry by less than 1 s is acknowledged and broadcasts nothing.

For allow-list tests, create the mock with `requestLog: true`: `mock.getRequestLog()` then returns every client frame with its session id and arrival time (the last 4096 frames, at most 8 MiB of JSON), with a string `authToken` shown as `<redacted>`. Without it the log stays empty. `session.dropFromNetwork()` loses a session abruptly.

The HTTP answers of §1a (403, 421, 503 and so on) are not simulated: the mock has no CONNECT request.

## Test messages that are not in the protocol yet [#test-messages-that-are-not-in-the-protocol-yet]

Two test seams let operator console tests (`client/src/operator/mock/`) add messages from change requests that are not in the protocol yet, without editing client files. Both skip the schema, so use them only in tests.

**Client messages in**: pass `onUnhandledClientMessage(message, context)` to `createMockServer`.

* It receives the decoded JSON object of a client message whose `type` is not a protocol client message type, after that session’s hello. Only the type name decides this.
* Answer with `context.reply(json)`, which sends to that session only. A `server.ack` or `server.error` reply must match the protocol schema, and its `replyTo` must be the incoming message’s `requestId`; other protocol message types are refused. Check a lease with `context.holdsLease(message.leaseId)`. `context.session` and `context.server` are also there.
* Return `false` to decline. The session then closes as malformed input, as it does without the hook.
* A message of a known type that fails its schema never reaches the hook: it closes the session as malformed input.
* A hook that throws closes that session.
* The hook may call `context.reply` and `mock.broadcast` while it runs; frames keep their order.

**Server messages out**: `mock.broadcast(json, filter?)` sends one control frame to every session past its hello, or only to the sessions `filter` selects.

* It returns `{ ok: true, sessions }`, or `{ ok: false, issue }` and sends nothing when the message has no string `type`, cannot be serialised as JSON (for example a `bigint`), exceeds the 1 MiB frame limit, or the filter throws.
* To select sessions by fields the client schema drops, read `session.helloJson`, a frozen copy of that session’s raw `client.hello` (null before the hello). For example, `(s) => s.helloJson?.role === 'operator'`.
* It refuses message types the protocol already defines (use the mock’s own controls, or `sendMalformed` for faults); it is only for types not in the protocol yet.
* It does not apply shared-update filtering and does not advance the metadata revision. For a message that carries `metadataRevision`, stamp it with `mock.advanceMetadataRevision()`.
* A normal client that receives a type it does not know fails that session with `unknown-message-type` and reconnects. So `broadcast` does not refuse operator message types; instead, operator tests always pass a filter that selects only operator sessions, and check that viewer sessions receive no operator messages.

To start the mock in setup with autocalibration, pass a snapshot with `readiness: 'needs-setup'`, `autocalibrate: true` and camera-pose `missing`. Media is held until camera-pose is committed, and the mock never starts a calibration by itself.

## What you should see [#what-you-should-see]

* A client connects and receives a snapshot. With a recording, it receives paired colour and depth frames after it subscribes.
* The setup lock is exclusive. It stays held while its owner heartbeats every 5 s, and it expires 15 s after the last heartbeat.
* A calibration result or placement update reaches clients that opted in to shared updates, and the client that made the change, as the message itself. Every other client gets a revision notice at the same revision in its place (change 0007). A placement commit is two revisions: the update, then a placement revision notice to every client. It restarts no media stream (change 0040).
* Each fault drives the client’s recovery path: a resync, a reconnect, or `resync-failed` followed by a reconnect.

In the browser, with the dev server running (`npm run dev` in `client/`):

* **The app**: in the side panel of [http://localhost:5173/](http://localhost:5173/), **Add mock server** under **Servers** adds a mock as a new server card, with the source `mock mock://dev-mock-…`.
  * It is snapshot-only (`snapshot only, no media`). Only where a local copy of the unpublished sample recordings exists in `client/reference/hevc-web/` does it serve them (`reference recording`); see [Sample recordings](/docs/client/developer/test-the-client#sample-recordings).
  * The section exists only in the dev server. A production build (`npm run build`) contains no mock code.
* **Both bundle layouts**: `src/tests/bundleLayouts.test.ts` plays a mock server in `per-camera` (one bundle per camera) and `concatenated` (one bundle, tiles side by side) layout with 1, 2 and 4 cameras. It checks the bundle and tile counts, that each camera's cloud lands at its own place, and that no pair is dropped. The decoder is synthetic: no HEVC is decoded.
* **Two clients of one mock**: the [cards check](/docs/client/developer/cards-check), [setup check](/docs/client/developer/setup-check) and [placement check](/docs/client/developer/placement-check) pages.

## Fix mock server problems [#fix-mock-server-problems]

* **`createMockServer` returns `ok: false`**: read `issues`. It needs a snapshot or a recording, the snapshot must be valid, and the snapshot’s lock must be free.
* **Nothing happens in a test**: a `ManualScheduler` only moves when you call `advanceBy` or `advanceTo`, and replies need a few microtask turns to settle.
* **No media**: check all of the following.
  * The mock needs a recording.
  * The client must subscribe, or list the bundle in `preferredBundleIds`.
  * The server must be `streaming`, with the bundle available.
  * If the snapshot has `autocalibrate` set, media is held until camera-pose is committed.
* **`skipRevisions` makes the client resync**: change 0007 makes any step other than +1 unexpected (§10). The client logs the gap, asks for one snapshot and stays connected. `sendStaleRevision` exercises the same path with a step backwards.

## Network sessions (CR 0018 H) [#network-sessions-cr-0018-h]

The `networkSensing` and `networkSessions` options script `server.network.sessions` for operator sessions: 0, 1, 3 or 64 rows and variants for null estimates, lower bounds, each confidence, unknown enums and stale client reports. Both are off by default. See [Network sensing](/docs/client/developer/network-sensing) for the options and examples.


# Network sensing (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/network-sensing)



Network sensing is the client side of [change request 0018](https://github.com/irc-hslu/orbbecstreamer/blob/main/protocol/changes/0018-network-calibration-stream.md) (protocol 1.2, feature `network-sensing`). It only measures and reports. It changes no bitrate, budget or encoder setting.

This page covers what is built: passive sensing (slice C2), the probe streams (slice C3) and the numbers on the viewer’s server card (slice C1 for the viewer). The adaptation that uses them is not built.

## What happens in a session [#what-happens-in-a-session]

1. The client lists `network-sensing` in `client.hello.features` and announces protocol 1.2. With probes on (the default with sensing in a runtime that carries media; the control-only runtime, `media: 'none'`, such as the Operator Console, keeps sensing and lists no probe feature unless `networkProbes: true` is passed) it also lists `network-probe` and `network-probe-c2s`. It never lists a probe feature without `network-sensing`, and drops one a caller passes on its own.
2. The server answers with `server.hello.features`. Sensing is on for the session only if **both** lists name it and the session counts as minor 2 or higher (the lower of the two announced minors).
3. Until then nothing is sent, and the server's `server.network.report` and `server.network.sessions` are ignored without being parsed. A malformed one is therefore not an error before the feature is negotiated.
4. Once on, the client sends a `client.network.report` once a second and parses the server's reports. A malformed report then fails that one connection with `invalid-message`. No other connection is affected.
5. When the session ends, the sensor stops, its timer is cancelled and the numbers are discarded. A reconnect negotiates again from the hello and starts at sequence 0.

A server older than minor 2, or one that does not list a feature, sees only extra feature strings and nothing else. A probe feature listed without `network-sensing`, by either side, counts as absent. Each probe direction is on only when sensing is negotiated and both sides listed that direction's feature.

Which runtimes offer it: the viewer app does. The Operator Console's control runtime passes `networkSensing: true` itself. `networkSensing: true | false` and `networkProbes: true | false` in the runtime options override this; `networkProbes` has no effect without sensing and defaults to off for a control-only runtime.

## What the client measures [#what-the-client-measures]

| Report field                                                                  | Source                                                                             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `s2c.arrivalRateBps`                                                          | Bytes returned by every read on the session (control, media, headers)              | A 5 s window. Always `lowerBound: true`: the server only sends what the encoder produces. One addition per read on the hot path.                                                                                                |
| `rtt.pingMinUs`                                                               | Minimum of the [clock sync](/docs/client/developer/latency) pings in the last 30 s | One ping every 10 s, so at most three samples: confidence is `low` or `medium` by construction.                                                                                                                                 |
| `rtt.smoothedUs`, `minUs`, `variationUs`                                      | `WebTransport.getStats()`, if the browser has it                                   | Stock Chrome 155 has no `getStats`. Behind `--enable-experimental-web-platform-features` it returns only these three RTT values, in milliseconds. The client converts them to whole microseconds.                               |
| `s2c.burstRateBps`                                                            | Dispersion of s→c probe trains and of large media records (below)                  | Median of the valid samples of the last 10 s. `basis` is `passive` (media samples only), `active` (probe samples only) or `mixed` (both); always `lowerBound: true`. `null` until a record or a train passes the validity test. |
| `s2c.bytesReceived`, `c2s.bytesSent`, `c2s.bytesLost` and the packet counters | `getStats()`, if the browser fills them                                            | Chrome 155 does not. They are `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Everything the browser cannot measure is `null`, never estimated:

* **Loss** in either direction. Only the server's sender sees s→c loss, and Chrome returns no c→s loss counters.
* **The client's own send rate** (`estimatedSendRateBps`). The browser's `estimatedSendRate` has no stated unit, so it is not used.
* **Queue delay** (`queueDelayP50Us`, `queueDelayP95Us`). It needs the 60 s baseline, which is not built.
* Anything while the page is hidden or media is suspended. Reads stall then, so the report says `suspended: true`, withholds the rate (`null`) and asks the server to hold probes (`holdProbes: true`, with `holdReasons` such as `hidden` or `suspended`).

**Burst rate from media records.** Every media record with a payload of at least 65536 bytes gives one dispersion sample, except a keyframe that is the first record of its stream. The rule is the probe trains' rule below: `8 x (B - b1) / (t_last - t1)` over the reads of the payload (the record header's bytes do not count), kept only with at least 4 reads, a first read of at most 25 % of `B` and no gap above 8 ms. The meter runs only in a session that negotiated `network-sensing`: one per media stream, one clock read per read (the arrival clock when there is one), no allocation per read or per record. Samples that arrive while the page is held are dropped by the sensor, as probe samples are.

`stats` says how much of `getStats` was usable: `unavailable` (no method, a failed call, or nothing usable), `partial` (some fields) or `available` (all nine the report can fill). No estimate and no decision depends on `getStats` being there.

## Probe streams (slice C3) [#probe-streams-slice-c3]

A probe train is one short unidirectional stream: a `network.probe.header`, exactly `trainBytes` bytes, then FIN. A browser can only time bytes it reads, which is why probes are streams.

**s→c (the server opens them; feature `network-probe`).** The first frame of every incoming unidirectional stream is its type tag: `media.channel.header` makes a media channel, `network.probe.header` a probe train, and any other well-formed type, or a probe header when the feature is off, cancels that one stream and logs a warning. A malformed header is fatal for the connection (`invalid-message`, or the framing code); the cross-field rules (direction must be `s2c`, `trainBytes` 16384..65536) are part of it. The payload is advisory: a short train, a reset, more bytes than declared, or a train unfinished 2 s after its header loses that one sample and nothing else. Reads use one reused 64 KiB buffer per session (BYOB) and keep only running aggregates: no buffer and no array grows per read (the browser's BYOB read hands back one small view object and a promise each time). One train is read at a time: its slot is free as soon as the last payload byte arrived, and the wait for the FIN goes on in the background, so the back-to-back trains of an episode are accepted; a train that starts while another is still being read is cancelled. The rate is `8 x (B - b1) / (t_last - t1)` and counts only if the train took at least 4 reads, the first read carried at most 25 % of it, and no gap between reads exceeded 8 ms. It is a lower bound, not capacity.

**c→s (the client opens them; feature `network-probe-c2s`).** One 32 KiB train of zeros, written in one go, at most one open stream, none in the first 30 s after `server.hello` (the state stays `passive`, so the first train goes at 30 s at the earliest), at least 30 s between trains (from the end of the previous one; a refused, failed or aborted train spaces the next like a good one), aborted if it is not done in 2 s. The 2 s covers opening the stream: a hung open returns the sender to `cooldown` at the deadline, and a stream that opens late is aborted unwritten. The gateway enforces the same caps before it reads. The client sends one only when the server's report has no `c2s.trainRateBps`, or the value is stale. The report has no timestamp for the value, so this is approximate: a value counts as fresh for 120 s after the client first saw it or saw it change (value, samples or window). The transport refuses to open the stream unless the feature was negotiated.

The state of the c→s probe is in the report (`c2s.probe`): `passive`, `probing`, `cooldown` or `held`, with `holdReasons`, `bytesLast60s`, `activeMsLast60s` and `lastProbeId`. It is `held` when an exclusion applies, and `passive` again after every exclusion has been clear for 5 s:

| Hold reason           | Condition on the client                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
