| Symptom                                                                                                                                                   | Cause and fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `preflight` shows `FAIL  nvidia-driver` or `FAIL  driver-libraries`                                                                                       | No NVIDIA driver 580 or newer. Install it (for example `sudo apt install nvidia-open`), reboot, and run `orbbec-streamer-preflight` again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `preflight` shows `FAIL  cuda-runtime` or `FAIL  tensorrt`                                                                                                | NVIDIA's apt repository is missing. Add it (step 2), then run the `sudo apt install` command in the `fix:` line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `WARN  orbbec-cameras`                                                                                                                                    | No camera is connected. Connect it to a USB 3 port.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The log repeats `No configured cameras are active`                                                                                                        | No camera was found when the cameras were opened (at service start only if `start_capture_on_launch: true`). The service retries with a growing delay and stops after 10 starts in 30 minutes. Connect the camera, then run `sudo systemctl reset-failed orbbec-streamer && sudo systemctl start orbbec-streamer`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| After an upgrade, the stats show `mask: failed` and the log shows an engine error, such as `Cannot open TensorRT engine: …`                               | You kept an edited `live.yaml` from poc.1 or poc.2, which names a fixed engine file. In the `mask:` section of `/etc/orbbec-streamer/live.yaml`, delete `rvm_engine_path` and set `rvm_onnx_path: "/usr/share/orbbec-streamer/models/rvm/rvm_mobilenetv3_b{batch}_640x576_ds0.5_float16.onnx"` and `rvm_engine_cache_dir: "/var/lib/orbbec-streamer/engines"`. Then run `sudo systemctl restart orbbec-streamer`; the first start builds the engine (3 to 4 minutes).                                                                                                    |
| The log shows `error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1`                                                                                        | The NVIDIA driver is missing. Install it and reboot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| The Femto Bolt doesn't start; the log shows depth engine error 204                                                                                        | The service can't use the GPU's render node. Check that `id orbbec-streamer` lists `render`; if not, run `sudo adduser orbbec-streamer render`, then `sudo systemctl restart orbbec-streamer`. Only if that doesn't help: run `sudo systemctl edit orbbec-streamer`, add the three lines `[Service]`, `DeviceAllow=` and `DevicePolicy=auto`, save and restart. The empty `DeviceAllow=` is needed: while the unit lists devices, `DevicePolicy=auto` alone changes nothing. This turns off the service's device allow-list, so remove it again once the cause is found. |
| The page at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` loads, but nothing connects                                                                                           | The server isn't running. From poc.10 the install starts it, unless a kept `live.yaml` sets `start_capture_on_launch: true`; up to poc.9 it doesn't. Run `sudo systemctl start orbbec-streamer`. Otherwise, up to poc.9 the gateway starts only once a camera is active, and the first start may still be building the engine. From poc.9 the gateway starts with the service; if the page connects but shows **Cameras closed**, select **Start cameras** on the server's card. Check `journalctl -u orbbec-streamer -f`.                                               |
| The server stops once, about 4 minutes after the first start, and starts again within seconds                                                             | Known issue in poc.7, fixed in poc.8: the stop comes when the segmentation engine build finishes. systemd restarts the server; no action needed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Several cameras: the page shows the server needs setup and no point cloud                                                                                 | The camera poses aren't calibrated. See [Calibrate the camera poses](/docs/operator#calibrate-the-camera-poses) (from poc.11) or [Camera pose calibration](/docs/server/camera-calibration).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Several cameras: the server stops after about 10 s with `no batch for 10005 ms …`, or refuses to start with `sync.enabled=false allows only one camera …` | Sync is off. See [More than one camera](#more-than-one-camera).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| The install printed `certificate setup postponed: the clock is not synchronised yet; the hourly renewal timer retries`                                    | The first certificates need a synchronised clock. Check that `timedatectl` shows `System clock synchronized: yes` (turn on NTP with `sudo timedatectl set-ntp true`), then run `sudo systemctl start orbbec-tls-renew.service`, or wait up to an hour for the timer. Until then no browser can connect.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Up to v0.1.4, on a PC without NTP: browsers stop connecting after about two weeks                                                                         | Renewal skipped every run while the clock wasn't synchronised, so the certificates expired. Upgrade to v0.1.5, or synchronise the clock and run `sudo systemctl start orbbec-tls-renew.service`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| From v0.1.5, `journalctl -u orbbec-tls-renew` says the clock is not synchronised and is earlier than, or more than 90 days after, the newest certificate  | Renewal waits instead of making certificates with a wrong date. Synchronise the clock, or, once it shows the right time, run `sudo /usr/lib/orbbec-streamer/tls/orbbec-tls --allow-unsynced renew`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `journalctl -u orbbec-tls-renew` names `regenerate-ca --yes`                                                                                              | The local certificate authority is damaged or no longer usable. Run `sudo /usr/lib/orbbec-streamer/tls/orbbec-tls regenerate-ca --yes`. Up to v0.1.4, add `--group orbbec-streamer --key-owner orbbec-streamer` before `regenerate-ca`; without them the keys get the wrong owner and the server can't read them. Every LAN viewer must then trust the new authority again (see [Remote viewers on the LAN](#remote-viewers-on-the-lan)). A damaged certificate or key other than the authority is replaced by itself from v0.1.5.                                       |
| The page doesn't load                                                                                                                                     | Check `systemctl status orbbec-streamer-web` and `journalctl -u orbbec-streamer-web`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Another computer can't open the page                                                                                                                      | LAN viewers are off by default. See [Remote viewers on the LAN](#remote-viewers-on-the-lan).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |


# Build the server from source (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/getting-started/install-server)



This is the minimal path for developers. To run OrbbecStreamer without
building it, use [Install the release package](/docs/getting-started/install-package)
instead. The [Server](/docs/server) section has the full
detail for every step, including every package, every troubleshooting
message, and how to build for a GPU other than the tested one.

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ## Check your machine [#check-your-machine]

    The tested machine is Ubuntu 26.04 with an NVIDIA RTX 4090 (compute
    capability 8.9), CUDA 13, TensorRT 11 and Orbbec cameras on USB 3. See
    [Requirements](/docs/server/requirements) for the full list and a check
    command for each item, including what to do on an older GPU.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Clone the repository [#clone-the-repository]

    ```bash
    git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:irc-hslu/orbbecstreamer.git
    cd orbbecstreamer/server
    ```

    Without a GitHub SSH key, see [Install](/docs/server/install#get-the-source)
    for the HTTPS form.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Install the system packages and SDKs [#install-the-system-packages-and-sdks]

    Follow [Install](/docs/server/install) start to finish: system packages,
    CUDA, TensorRT, the Orbbec SDK and vcpkg. The RVM segmentation engine near
    the end is optional; skip it for now.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Configure and build [#configure-and-build]

    ```bash
    cmake --preset dev-debug
    cmake --build --preset debug
    ```

    The first configure builds every vcpkg dependency from source and can take
    a long time. The presets set the compiler, CUDA and library-path variables
    for you; see
    [Environment variables](/docs/server/configuration#environment-variables)
    for the full list. See [Build and test](/docs/server/build) for the Makefile
    shortcuts, the CTest labels, CLion setup, and how to build for a GPU below
    compute capability 8.9.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Verify [#verify]

    ```bash
    ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --cuda-test
    ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --nvenc-test
    ```

    **Expected result:** `--cuda-test` reports your GPU and ends
    `CUDA smoke test OK`; `--nvenc-test` reports `main10=true` and ends
    `NVENC capability test passed`. See
    [Build and test](/docs/server/build#expected-result) for the full output on
    the reference machine, and its
    [Troubleshooting](/docs/server/build#troubleshooting) table for every
    failure message.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Next: [First stream](/docs/getting-started/first-stream). Want the browser
client too? See [Run the client](/docs/client/dev-build).


# Calibration (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/guides/calibration)



There are four calibration kinds. Each one is a server-side state; a client
can show it and, for some kinds, run it over a browser session. From
v0.1.0-poc.7 the session also carries live video (see
[Serve to browsers](/docs/server/serving)); up to poc.6 it carries status and
setup commands only. The team has not yet checked depth calibration on a
live scene on real hardware.

From v0.1.6 the camera-pose run keeps views by itself while the board is
held still, sorts them by distance, tilt and image region, and detects the
board in each camera's own colour image; the Operator Console shows each
camera's live image with the detected board. See
[Run a calibration](/docs/server/camera-calibration#run-a-calibration) and
[Calibrate the camera poses](/docs/operator#calibrate-the-camera-poses).
These changes were tested in simulation, not yet on hardware.

From v0.1.6 the server solves all camera poses together (a joint rig
adjustment) and checks the result against targets: 0.5 px reprojection
error and 10 mm between the cameras of each pair. In simulation, the joint
solution came within 0.12° and 2.7 to 3.7 mm of the truth. The programme's
goal is 0.1° and 2 mm; this is not met yet and has to be validated on the
rig. Every figure is simulated.

The Operator Console doesn't show the quality figures yet. After a run,
`journalctl -u orbbec-streamer` has one line for the run and one per
camera and per pair, and each commit writes
`/var/lib/orbbec-streamer/calibration/camera-pose.report.json`. Short
codes called advisories flag a calibration you shouldn't trust as it is,
for example `solved-before-warm-up` when a camera had streamed for less
than 40 minutes: let the cameras warm up before you calibrate. See
[Quality figures in the log](/docs/server/camera-calibration#quality-figures-in-the-log) and
[Advisories](/docs/server/camera-calibration#advisories).

| Kind               | On the server                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | From a browser, against a real server                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Camera pose        | One camera needs none: from v0.1.0-poc.7 the server writes its identity pose at start. Several cameras: works from the local console with a ChArUco board, tested with synthetic cameras and not yet validated on hardware. See [Camera pose calibration](/docs/server/camera-calibration). | The server accepts a camera-pose run from a client that holds the setup lock. With `autocalibrate: false` (the packaged default) that only re-runs a pose that is already valid, unless the session has the operator role. From v0.1.0-poc.11, the Operator Console has the operator role on the server PC and calibrates a missing pose; see [Calibrate the camera poses](/docs/operator#calibrate-the-camera-poses). Up to poc.10, a missing pose must be calibrated on the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Depth quantization | Works from a CLI tool. See [Depth quantization calibrator](/docs/server/depth-quantization-calibrator).                                                                                                                                                                                     | The server runs it for a client that holds the setup lock (since v0.1.0-poc.4): it samples live, masked depth, and a solved run waits for a commit, which swaps the new profile in without a restart. From v0.1.0-poc.6, the client can also commit the run against a real server: it follows the server's "solved; awaiting commit" behaviour. This was tested against the mock server; a check on real hardware is pending. With poc.5, the client can start, watch and cancel a run but not commit it, so use the calibrator or `orbbec-console calibrate depth --commit` (see [Terminal console](/docs/operator/terminal-console#calibrate-from-a-script)). The full flow works against the client's [mock server](/docs/client/developer/mock-server). See [Calibrate depth](/docs/client/calibration#depth-quantization). |
| Floor              | From v0.1.6 the server measures the floor plane from the running cameras; it needs a valid camera pose. Tested in simulation, not yet on hardware.                                                                                                                                          | From v0.1.6, a session with the operator role and the setup lock measures and commits it: in the Operator Console, see [Measure the floor](/docs/operator#measure-the-floor); in the client's setup workspace, see [Calibrate the floor](/docs/client/calibrate-floor). **Level to floor** turns the result into a placement draft that you commit yourself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Network            | Not available. A stream is reserved in the wire format, but no calibration procedure exists yet.                                                                                                                                                                                            | Not available.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### Before a depth run from a browser [#before-a-depth-run-from-a-browser]

The server refuses to start a depth run, with `calibration-unavailable`
and a reason, when:

* no capture is active (no camera is delivering frames);
* `mask.backend` or `processing.depth_filter_backend` is `none`;
* the person-mask engine is still being built on the first start, or has
  failed. Masks then pass every pixel, so the profile would include the
  background. Wait until the mask engine is ready, or set
  `mask.backend: fill_all` to calibrate on all depth.

From poc.6, a run needs at least four frames' worth of valid depth in one
camera's depth image; below that it keeps collecting, and fails at the
deadline with `too few valid depth samples …`. Point the cameras at the
scene, or widen the configured range (`encoding.depth.minimum_depth_mm`
and `maximum_depth_mm` in `live.yaml`). With poc.4 and poc.5 there is no
minimum, so check **valid samples** before you commit. Only one calibration run of any kind runs at a time. Cancelling, releasing
the lock or disconnecting abandons the run and keeps the profile in force.

The [Operator Console](/docs/operator) shows each kind's state under
**Calibration** on its Overview. From poc.6, its **Depth range calibration** screen (**Depth
calibration plot** in the navigation from v0.1.4) also runs and commits a depth-quantization calibration: see
[Calibrate the depth range](/docs/operator#calibrate-the-depth-range). The
[terminal console](/docs/operator/terminal-console#calibrate-from-a-script)
does the same from a script with `orbbec-console calibrate depth --commit`.

## Run calibration today [#run-calibration-today]

Run camera pose and depth quantization on the server:

1. With several cameras, calibrate the camera pose. From v0.1.0-poc.11, use
   the Operator Console; see
   [Calibrate the camera poses](/docs/operator#calibrate-the-camera-poses).
   Up to poc.10, use the server console with `--calibrate-camera-pose`; see
   [Camera pose calibration](/docs/server/camera-calibration). With one
   camera, poc.7 and later skip this step.
2. Optionally, build a depth quantization profile with the calibrator. See
   [Depth quantization calibrator](/docs/server/depth-quantization-calibrator).
   Without one, the server uses a linear depth range.
3. Start the server. A browser connected to it sees the committed result:
   the server card's **Pose** and **Depth** chips, or the console's
   Overview.
4. Optionally, from v0.1.6, measure the floor and level the placement to
   it; see [Measure the floor](/docs/operator#measure-the-floor). The
   client's server card then shows a **Floor** chip, for example
   `Floor valid · r2`.

[First stream](/docs/getting-started/first-stream) has a config already set
up for your cameras.


# From a fresh install to a fused point cloud (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/guides/fresh-start-to-fused-cloud)















{/* SKELETON for the core release (operator/design/release-core.md, M7).
    Not for publication until every step is filled and has been followed
    literally on a fresh rig install. Each TODO names the milestone that
    fills it. Quote strings from source at the release tag. */}

This guide takes one rig from a fresh install to a live, fused point cloud
in the browser and in the Operator Console preview. Follow the steps in
order; each one ends with what you should see.

## Before you start [#before-you-start]

{/* TODO M7: supported rig (PC, GPU, driver, cameras, sync cables, ChArUco
    board), from the release's hardware list. */}

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ## Install the package [#install-the-package]

    Follow [Install the release package](/docs/getting-started/install-package):
    check the machine, add NVIDIA's apt repository, install the `.deb`, run
    `orbbec-streamer-preflight`. The install starts the server with the
    cameras closed.

    You should see a last line starting `preflight: OK` at the end of the machine check. The first
    start builds the segmentation engine for your GPU, about 3 minutes, once.
    The cameras stay closed until you open them in the next steps.
    Until then the server's card reads **Cameras closed** and the Operator
    Console's Cameras panel reads `Cameras are closed. Start the cameras to see
    them here.` See [Cameras closed](/docs/operator#cameras-closed).
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Open the Operator Console [#open-the-operator-console]

    In Chrome or Edge on the server PC, open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/operator`
    (`http://localhost:8080/operator` works too). See
    [Operator Console](/docs/operator).

    You should see the page connect without asking for an address or a
    certificate, then the top bar chips **Connected** and **Setup lock: free**,
    and **Ready** or **Needs setup**. On the server PC the session has the
    [operator role](/docs/operator#the-operator-role), so the first chip reads
    **Settings and depth range · v… · protocol …**. If instead a banner reads
    **Opened as viewer**, the sensor and profile screens are read-only; the
    banner names the cause.

        <img alt="Operator Console Overview: Connected, Setup lock: free, Ready and Streaming, one camera connected with sync OK, and a hint that the depth range is not calibrated" src="__img0" />

    *Captured on 2026-10-17 from v0.1.2 installed from the package, with its default `live.yaml` (one Femto Bolt, sync off); the room was dark.*
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Check the cameras and their sync [#check-the-cameras-and-their-sync]

    Open the cameras first. In the Operator Console, select **Start cameras**
    on **Overview** or **Cameras & sync**; it reads **Starting cameras…** for up
    to a minute. See [Cameras closed](/docs/operator#cameras-closed). (The
    server's card in the client at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` has the same button;
    see [Server card](/docs/client/server-card).) If it reports that the
    cameras did not start, read the reason, check the camera's cable and power,
    and select **Start cameras** again.

    The default config runs one camera. For a rig, add each camera's serial
    number, mark exactly one as primary, connect the sync cables and set
    `sync.enabled: true`. The comments at the top of
    `/etc/orbbec-streamer/live.yaml` show how; your edits survive upgrades. See
    [More than one camera](/docs/getting-started/install-package#more-than-one-camera).

    In the Operator Console, open **Cameras & sync**. You should see one row
    for every camera, each **Connected** with health **OK**. In the
    **Setup checklist**, the **Cameras** step checks that every camera is
    connected on a good link and captures in sync. See
    [What each panel shows](/docs/operator#what-each-panel-shows).

        <img alt="Cameras & sync with one Femto Bolt: Connected, health OK, USB 3, sync role Standalone" src="__img1" />

    *Captured on 2026-10-17 from v0.1.2 installed from the package, with its default `live.yaml` (one Femto Bolt, sync off); the room was dark. The serial number is blurred.*

    In the first minute after **Start cameras**, a camera's health can read
    **Degraded**: the camera drops a few frame sets at each start while it
    syncs its clock. That is normal; it turns **OK** by itself.

    {/* TODO M4: hardware-sync status row and its healthy values (the console
        shows it as Not reported until protocol change 0029); what to do when a
        camera is out of sync. */}
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Apply sensor and profile settings [#apply-sensor-and-profile-settings]

    The defaults are already applied, so this step is a review. In the
    Operator Console, select **Take setup lock** on a settings screen, then
    look at **Colour sensor**, **Depth sensor** and **Stream profile** in the
    left navigation. Change only what your scene needs, and select **Leave
    setup** when you are done. See
    [Change sensor settings and the stream profile](/docs/operator#change-sensor-settings-and-the-stream-profile).

    * On **Colour sensor** and **Depth sensor**, the **All cameras** tab reaches
      every camera. Sliders apply when you let go of them; **Applied:** shows
      the value the camera really took.
    * On **Stream profile**, choose a row in **Stream profiles**, select
      **Apply profile**, then **Apply and restart streams**. Streams pause for a
      few seconds.

    With person segmentation on (the default), v0.1.2 to v0.1.4 offer only the 640×576
    depth profiles; see the
    [known issue](/docs/operator#change-sensor-settings-and-the-stream-profile).

    You should see the **Sensors** and **Profiles** steps of the **Setup
    checklist** (see [The setup checklist](/docs/operator#the-setup-checklist))
    without errors, and `Settings are kept by the server for each camera and
    restored after a restart.` on the sensor screens.

        <img alt="Colour sensor, read-only until you take the setup lock: Auto exposure on, Exposure 200, Gain 0, Auto white balance on" src="__img2" />

        <img alt="Stream profile: the current profile, 640x576 depth, 1280x720 colour, 15 fps, above the profiles you can switch to" src="__img3" />

    *Captured on 2026-10-17 from v0.1.2 installed from the package, with its default `live.yaml` (one Femto Bolt, sync off); the room was dark.*

    {/* TODO M4: first-run wizard, expected time about 5 minutes; screenshots of
        the sensor and profile screens. */}
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Calibrate the depth range [#calibrate-the-depth-range]

    This step is optional. Without it the server uses a linear depth range.
    Follow [Calibrate the depth range](/docs/operator#calibrate-the-depth-range):
    on **Depth calibration plot** (**Depth range** up to v0.1.3), select **Take setup lock**, then **Start depth-range
    calibration**, and have one person walk through the whole capture volume,
    near and far. The cameras must be running and the segmentation engine
    ready; see [Calibration](/docs/guides/calibration#before-a-depth-run-from-a-browser).

    You should see **Elapsed**, **Valid samples**, **Observed range** and
    **Reconstruction error** update for about a minute, then **Result ready**
    with **Not in force until committed**. Check **Valid samples** and
    **Reconstruction error**, select **Commit result**, and wait for
    **Committed · revision N**. Select **Leave setup**.

    {/* TODO M2: confirm on the rig with a live scene; real screenshot. */}
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Calibrate the camera poses [#calibrate-the-camera-poses]

    With one camera, skip this step: the server writes the camera's identity
    pose at its first start. You should see **Pose valid · r1** on the server's
    card.

    With several cameras, the server needs a camera-pose calibration before it
    sends video. Print the ChArUco board that the **Camera pose** screen
    describes: from v0.1.4 the screen draws it, and **Download board (SVG,
    print at 100 %)** saves it at its real size (see also
    [Camera pose calibration](/docs/server/camera-calibration)). The default
    from v0.1.4 is 4 × 6 squares of 105 mm; see
    [Calibration board](/docs/getting-started/install-package#calibration-board).
    Fix it to something rigid and flat. One person moves the
    board.

    In the Operator Console, open **Camera pose** under **Calibration**, select
    **Take setup lock**, then **Start camera-pose calibration**. From v0.1.6,
    start only after the cameras have streamed for about 40 minutes: their
    depth drifts while they warm up, and the server flags a pose solved
    earlier (`solved-before-warm-up`). From v0.1.6
    each camera's tile shows its live image with the detected board drawn on
    it and `Board seen (N corners)`; hold the board still for a moment at each
    spot so the server keeps the view, then move or tilt it to a new one. Move the board
    as the screen's instruction says, until every highlighted region of every
    camera is covered and **Camera links** joins all cameras. When the screen
    shows **Proposed camera pose**, select **Commit camera pose**, then
    **Leave setup**. See
    [Calibrate the camera poses](/docs/operator#calibrate-the-camera-poses).

    You should see **Camera pose committed (revision N)** and `The new poses
    are in force.`, and the top bar change from **Needs setup** to **Ready**.
    The **Calibration** step of the **Setup checklist** shows the same screen;
    see [The setup checklist](/docs/operator#the-setup-checklist). The team
    has tested this calibration with synthetic cameras only, not yet on
    hardware.

        <img alt="Camera pose calibration with one camera: Camera pose: valid · revision 1, the ChArUco board description and Start camera-pose calibration" src="__img4" />

    *Captured on 2026-10-17 from v0.1.2 installed from the package, with its default `live.yaml` (one Femto Bolt, sync off); the room was dark. The pose shown is the identity pose the server writes for one camera; no board calibration was run.*

    {/* TODO M2: real screenshots from the rig run (B3), two cameras with a board. */}
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Start streaming and watch the preview [#start-streaming-and-watch-the-preview]

    If the cameras are still closed, select **Start cameras** on the Operator
    Console's **Overview**. Then open **Preview** in
    the Operator Console's left navigation (`/operator/preview`) and choose
    **Cloud**. See [Watch the live preview](/docs/operator#watch-the-live-preview).
    For the client itself, see [First stream](/docs/getting-started/first-stream).

    You should see the server's card read **Streaming**, and in the
    **Preview** the cameras' points drawn in 3D, with **Pause drawing**,
    **Frame all** and **Reset view**. **Colour tiles** and **Depth tiles** show
    each camera's pictures, and the table below shows frame sets per second,
    decode latency and dropped frame sets. While a tile has no picture it reads
    **Waiting for first frame**. The preview needs WebGPU and an HEVC decoder;
    see [Check your browser](/docs/client/browser-requirements). If WebGPU
    can't draw, the preview uses WebGL2 and shows a notice
    with a **What to do** link; see
    [When WebGPU can't draw](/docs/client/browser-requirements#when-webgpu-cant-draw).

    {/* TODO M1: real (not test-pattern) preview screenshots; what a correct
        fused cloud looks like. */}
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Connect a viewer [#connect-a-viewer]

    On the server PC, open `http://127.0.0.1:8080` and connect to the server;
    see [First stream](/docs/getting-started/first-stream).

    To view from another computer on the same LAN, turn on LAN viewers as in
    [Remote viewers on the LAN](/docs/getting-started/install-package#remote-viewers-on-the-lan):
    the page server's drop-in, `lan_viewers: true` in `live.yaml`, the
    firewall ports, and the installation's certificate authority trusted once
    on each viewer. Then open `https://<server-hostname>.local:8443` on the
    viewer. A LAN viewer never gets the operator role: it can open the
    Operator Console at `/operator` only as a viewer. From v0.1.6 a viewer
    can't take the setup lock or calibrate the depth range; up to v0.1.5 it
    could.

    You should see the same point cloud on the viewer as in the console's
    **Preview**.

    {/* TODO M6: confirm from a second machine on the rig run; real screenshot. */}
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Measure the floor (optional) [#measure-the-floor-optional]

    From v0.1.6 the server can measure the floor from the running cameras, so
    that the scene stands level in the viewer. It needs a valid camera pose and
    the operator role. In the Operator Console, open **Floor** under
    **Calibration**, select **Take setup lock**, then **Measure floor**. When
    the screen reads `Solved. Not in force until committed.`, select **Commit
    floor**. Then select **Level to floor**: it opens a placement draft, which
    you commit with **Commit placement (expected revision N)**. Nothing is
    levelled without that commit. See
    [Measure the floor](/docs/operator#measure-the-floor). The floor
    measurement was tested in simulation, not yet on hardware.

    You should see `Floor: measured · revision N` and, in the client with
    **Show floor** on in the view settings, the floor grid under the scene.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Check the network [#check-the-network]

    From v0.1.1, open **Network** in the Operator Console's left navigation
    (`/operator/network`). See
    [The Operator Console's Network panel](/docs/guides/network#the-operator-consoles-network-panel).

    You should see one row for each connected session, your own marked
    **You**, with round-trip time, the rates in both directions and loss from
    the server to each viewer. A `≥` before a rate means the real value is at
    least that high; see [Read the estimates](/docs/guides/network#read-the-estimates).

        <img alt="The Network panel with two loopback sessions, the console (Operator, You) and one viewer, with rates, round-trip time and loss" src="__img5" />

    *Captured on 2026-10-17 from v0.1.2 installed from the package, with its default `live.yaml` (one Femto Bolt, sync off); the room was dark. The viewer tab received no video, so **Media, Mbit/s** reads `— not measured`.*

    {/* TODO M6: the rig's healthy values, loopback and LAN viewer; screenshot. */}
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ## Add a second server and place it [#add-a-second-server-and-place-it]

    {/* TODO M5 (in core, last; owner 2026-10-12): multi-server fusion and placement; see
        [Placement](/docs/guides/placement). */}
  </Step>
</Steps>

# Network sensing (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/guides/network)







**Network sensing** is how OrbbecStreamer learns about the network between
a server and a viewer. It only measures and reports. It does not change the
bitrate, the encoder settings or what the server sends.

It is part of protocol 1.2 (change 0018), from v0.1.1. It works only
between a server and a viewer that both support it. A viewer or server without it sees nothing new.

## How it works [#how-it-works]

Sensing is **passive**. Each side works out its numbers from traffic that
already flows: the connection's own statistics, the media it receives, and
the regular round-trip checks between viewer and server. It sends no extra
test traffic.

It is **periodic**. Each side sends a report about once a second, and an
extra one when a number moves a lot. A side never sends more than four
reports a second.

It runs in **both directions**:

* The server measures towards each viewer: round-trip time, how much data
  it got through to that viewer, and how much was lost on the way.
* Each viewer reports back what it sees: round-trip time, how fast data
  arrives, and how long data waits in the network.

Loopback, local network and remote viewers are measured the same way.

A viewer only sees the numbers for its own connection. The
[Operator Console](/docs/operator) is meant to show every viewer's numbers
side by side. No viewer gets another viewer's numbers or an address.

## Read the estimates [#read-the-estimates]

Every number comes with a few words that say how far to trust it.

| Word                                | What it tells you                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Lower bound                         | The real value is at least this high. The Operator Console shows "≥" before the value.          |
| Confidence: `low`, `medium`, `high` | How steady the recent samples were. It says nothing about whether the number is the true limit. |
| Not measured                        | No valid value. It is never guessed.                                                            |

### Lower bound [#lower-bound]

Most rates are lower bounds. The server only sends as much as the cameras
produce, so a rate it reaches is not the most the path could carry. The
rate at which data arrives at a viewer is always a lower bound, and so is
the burst rate.

Treat a number as the path's real capacity only if it is not a lower bound
and its confidence is `medium` or `high`.

### Confidence [#confidence]

Confidence is about **precision**, not accuracy. Over the last few seconds,
`high` needs at least 5 samples that agree closely. `medium` needs at least
3 that agree fairly well. Anything else is `low`.

A `high` lower bound is a steady number that is still only a floor.
A `low` number may just be new: a connection that started a moment ago has
few samples.

### Not measured [#not-measured]

A number that is "not measured" has no valid samples yet, or can't be
measured on that side. Some are only missing at first. For example, the
loss figure needs data to have been sent in the window.

## What a browser can't measure [#what-a-browser-cant-measure]

A browser tab can see less of the connection than the server can. These
stay "not measured" on the viewer side, whatever the network does:

* **Packet loss, in either direction.** Only the server's sending side sees
  loss, so loss is reported for the server-to-viewer direction only.
  Viewer-to-server loss isn't measured at all.
* **The viewer's own sending rate** and the capacity of the viewer-to-server
  path. The server reports how fast it receives data from the viewer. That is
  a sanity check, not a capacity figure.
* **Connection internals** such as congestion window, data in flight,
  acknowledgement timing and congestion marks.
* **Anything while the tab is hidden.** A browser slows hidden tabs, which
  would look like a network collapse. The viewer marks the report as
  suspended instead of reporting a drop.

Some browsers expose connection statistics and some don't. Sensing doesn't
depend on them: round-trip time from the regular checks and the rates from
arriving media always work.

## The Operator Console's Network panel [#the-operator-consoles-network-panel]

The **Network** panel (`/operator/network`, in the left navigation) shows
the estimates for every session connected to the server, one row each. Only
sessions with the [operator role](/docs/operator#the-operator-role) see it;
open the console on the server PC. Your own session is marked **You**.

<img alt="The Network panel with five sessions: role, peer, the rates in both directions, round-trip time, loss, queue delay and report age for each" src="__img0" />

*Captured against the client's mock server, so the sessions and figures are made up.*

The columns are **Session**, **Role**, **Peer**, **Server to client rate
(approx.), Mbit/s**, **Media, Mbit/s**, **Client to server rate, Mbit/s**,
**RTT smoothed / min, ms**, **Loss s→c, %**, **Queue delay p95, ms** and
**Report age**. The small bars after a number show its confidence. Select
**+** on a row for its **Measurement details**.

From v0.1.2, **Media, Mbit/s** shows the rate of media the server hands to
the session's connection; with v0.1.1 it reads `— not measured`. It is what
the server sends, not what the path could carry. Nothing acts on these
numbers yet.

<img alt="A session's measurement details: each measure with its lower-bound mark, confidence and number of samples" src="__img1" />

How to read the cells:

| You see                | Meaning                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `≥` before a value     | A lower bound: the real value is at least this high. Screen readers say "at least". |
| `— not measured`       | No valid estimate yet, or one the browser can't give.                               |
| `not reporting`        | The session's client sends no network reports, for example an older client.         |
| `no client report yet` | The client reports, but its first report hasn't arrived.                            |
| `unknown`              | The server sent a value this console doesn't know.                                  |

**Loss s→c** is only the loss from the server to the viewer: the browser
doesn't expose the loss in the other direction.

On **Overview**, the Network row sums it up as `N sessions · worst RTT … ·
worst loss …`, with the same `≥` and `(low confidence)` marks.

Other messages on the panel:

| Message                                                                          | Meaning                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `This server does not report network numbers. It needs protocol 1.2 or later; …` | The server is v0.1.0 or older. Update the server, then reload. |
| `Waiting for network telemetry`                                                  | The panel has opened and the first report hasn't arrived yet.  |
| `Network telemetry stopped arriving. Values shown are as of …`                   | Reports stopped; the numbers are from that time.               |
| `The server lists at most 64 sessions. More may be connected and are not shown.` | The server caps the list.                                      |
| `No other sessions are connected.`                                               | Only this console is connected.                                |

## Active probes [#active-probes]

Active probes are short, deliberate bursts of test data that fill gaps when
passive data is thin. The server has them from v0.1.1 and the browser
client from v0.1.2, but they are **off by default**: the server offers them
to no session and sends no probe traffic.

The packaged `/etc/orbbec-streamer/live.yaml` lists the key commented
out. To try probes, set it under `serving:` and run
`sudo systemctl restart orbbec-streamer`:

```yaml
serving:
  network_probes: true
```

Leave them off. They are for the team's two-host measurements, which have
not passed yet, and they add traffic on top of the live streams. The
release notes say when the default changes.

A server older than v0.1.1 doesn't know the key and refuses to start with
`Unsupported serving key: network_probes`. Before you downgrade, delete
the line from `live.yaml`.

## See also [#see-also]

* [Operator Console](/docs/operator)
* [Network reports on the server](/docs/server/serving#network-reports-protocol-12)


# Placement (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/guides/placement)



A server's **placement** is a rigid transform (a translation plus a
rotation) that says where its point cloud sits relative to a named anchor.
Once committed, every client draws that server's cloud there.

## The flow [#the-flow]

1. **Take the setup lock.** Open the server's [setup workspace](/docs/client/setup-workspace)
   with **Set up** on its card. From v0.1.6 this needs the
   [operator role](/docs/operator#the-operator-role), so use a browser on
   the server PC.
2. **Edit.** In the workspace's Placement section, select **Edit**, then change the pose with
   numeric fields or by dragging a 3D handle on the cloud. This only changes
   a local draft in your browser; nothing is sent yet. See
   [Place a server in the scene](/docs/client/placement-editing).
3. **Commit.** Select **Commit**. Once the server accepts it, the
   placement's revision goes up by one and every connected client redraws
   the cloud at the new pose. See
   [Commit or discard the draft](/docs/client/placement-editing#commit-or-discard-the-draft).

This is separate from a **world anchor**, which is where an anchor sits in
*your own* browser's scene: local to you, never sent anywhere. See
[Move an anchor in your view](/docs/client/world-anchors).

## What the server does with a commit today [#what-the-server-does-with-a-commit-today]

A real server accepts a placement commit over a browser session from the
client that holds the setup lock, as long as the placement is still at the
revision the draft started from. It saves the new placement to
`calibration.placement_path` before any client sees it, and restores it at
the next start (see the [`calibration` keys](/docs/server/configuration#calibration)).
With `placement_path: ""`, the placement is kept in memory only and resets
at every restart.

From v0.1.0-poc.7 the server sends live video, so you see your own
camera's point cloud while you edit the placement (see
[Serve to browsers](/docs/server/serving)). With poc.6 and earlier you edit
it without video. A placement commit doesn't interrupt the video. To try the
editor without a server, use the client's built-in mock server: see
[Mock server](/docs/client/developer/mock-server) and
[Placement check](/docs/client/developer/placement-check).


# Introduction (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs)



OrbbecStreamer captures colour and depth from Orbbec cameras, processes and
HEVC-encodes them on an NVIDIA GPU, and streams them over WebTransport to a
browser client.

From v0.1.0-poc.7 a browser on the server PC shows live video: the server
sends colour and depth to each browser that subscribes (see
[Serve to browsers](/docs/server/serving)), and the client draws point clouds
from them, as it does from [recordings](/docs/client/playback). With one
camera, a fresh install streams with no setup step. A first stream means
installing the [release package](/docs/getting-started/install-package),
starting the server and opening the client on the server PC: see
[First stream](/docs/getting-started/first-stream).
