`mask.rvm_onnx_path` already points at the exported files. The batch size must
equal the number of active cameras: batch 1 for one camera, batch 2 for two;
the server picks the file with `{batch}` in the path. For other values, see
`uv run python scripts/setup_rvm.py --help`.

The RVM model and weights are GPL-3.0. Confirm that this licence suits you
before you distribute the model or an engine built from it.

## First start [#first-start]

One camera needs no calibration: on the first start the server writes the
identity camera pose itself. Several cameras need a calibration first; run the
server with `--calibrate-camera-pose` (see
[Camera pose calibration](./camera-calibration)).

## Expected result [#expected-result]

`make check-env` prints your toolchain. On the reference machine:

```text
Compiler:
c++ (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0

CMake:
cmake version 4.1.2

Ninja:
1.13.2

CUDA:
/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc
Build cuda_13.3.r13.3/compiler.38244171_0

NVIDIA driver/GPU:
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 580.178.04
```

After the Orbbec SDK install, this command lists both files without an error:

```bash
ls /usr/local/lib/OrbbecSDKConfig.cmake /etc/udev/rules.d/99-obsensor-libusb.rules
```

After the optional RVM step, `models/rvm/generated/` contains:

```text
rvm_mobilenetv3_b1_640x576_ds0.5_float16.onnx
rvm_mobilenetv3_b2_640x576_ds0.5_float16.onnx
```

None of these files are committed. Without `--skip-engine-build` the folder
also holds the prebuilt `.engine` files with a `.json` manifest and a timing
cache for each, and the script ends with `RVM setup complete.` The engines the
server builds itself go to `mask.rvm_engine_cache_dir`, not here.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

| Symptom                                                                                                 | Cause and fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)` while fetching submodules                               | No GitHub SSH key is set up. Fetch the submodules over HTTPS with the `insteadOf` command in [Get the source](#get-the-source).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `make check-env` stops after `CUDA:` with `make: *** [Makefile:…: check-env] Error 1`                   | `/usr/local/cuda/bin` is not on your `PATH`. Do step 4 of [CUDA toolkit and driver](#cuda-toolkit-and-driver), then open a new shell.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `setup_rvm.py` fails with `source directory exists but is not a Git checkout`                           | The RVM submodule is not initialised, so `external/RobustVideoMatting` is an empty folder. Initialise the submodules as in [Get the source](#get-the-source).                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Configure fails with `Could NOT find TensorRT (missing: TensorRT_INCLUDE_DIR TensorRT_NVINFER_LIBRARY)` | Install `tensorrt-dev`, or set `TensorRT_ROOT` (or `TENSORRT_ROOT`) to a tar install. Then configure again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Configure fails with `Could not find a package configuration file provided by "OrbbecSDK"`              | The Orbbec SDK is missing or not in `/usr/local/lib`. Reinstall the `.deb`, or pass `-DOrbbecSDK_DIR=<folder that contains OrbbecSDKConfig.cmake>` to `cmake --preset dev-debug`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Configure fails with a pkg-config error that names `ffnvcodec`                                          | Install `libffmpeg-nvenc-dev`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Configure fails on `libavcodec`, `libavformat`, `libavutil` or `libswscale`                             | Install the matching `-dev` package from [System packages](#system-packages).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `dpkg -l tensorrt-dev` shows a `+cuda13.4` version                                                      | apt installed the newest TensorRT, which targets CUDA 13.4 and is not tested. To stay on the tested stack, pin every TensorRT package to `11.1.0.106-1+cuda13.3` with `sudo apt install <package>=11.1.0.106-1+cuda13.3` for `tensorrt-dev` and each `libnvinfer*` and `libnvonnxparsers*` package it depends on. This pinning has not been tested on a fresh machine. |
| `setup_rvm.py` fails with `trtexec not found; install libnvinfer-bin or pass --trtexec`                 | You did not pass `--skip-engine-build`. Pass it (the server builds its own engine), or install `libnvinfer-bin`, or pass `--trtexec /path/to/trtexec`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `setup_rvm.py` fails with `missing Python packages: ...`                                                | Run it with `uv run`, or add `--install-python-deps` inside a virtual environment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `setup_rvm.py` fails with `not an orbbec-streamer repository root`                                      | Run it from `server/`, or pass `--repo-root <path to server/>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| A camera works as root but not as your user                                                             | The udev rule is missing. Run `sudo /opt/OrbbecSDK_v2.8.7/shared/install_udev_rules.sh`, then replug the camera.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |


# Run two servers on one host (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/multi-server)



A client fuses several rigs by connecting to one server per rig and laying out each server's per-camera clouds with that server's committed placement (`protocol/wire-format.md` §7, §9, §14, §18). The server side is plain: each instance is an ordinary single-server run. This page covers running two on one machine, for example one camera per instance.

**Version.** Versions up to 0.1.1 cannot run two instances on one machine with real cameras. Enumeration opened every connected camera, so the second instance failed with `camera enumeration failed: uvc_open failed ... Return Code: -6` (the camera is busy) and stayed in `NEEDS_SETUP`, whichever instance started first. From 0.1.2 enumeration reads each camera's serial number from the device list without opening it, and only the camera named by `serial_number` is opened. A busy camera that is not yours no longer matters. If the camera you configured is busy, the instance fails and names its serial number and USB port.

## What each instance must own [#what-each-instance-must-own]

Instances share nothing at run time; everything below is set in the instance's own config. Example configs for two instances are in `server/config/multi-server/` (`rig-a.yaml`, `rig-b.yaml`).

| Resource                    | Setting                                                                                                                                                                                 | Rule                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Camera                      | `cameras[].serial_number`                                                                                                                                                               | One serial per instance. Opening a device is exclusive.                                                                                                          |
| WebTransport and page ports | `serving.listen_address`, `serving.page_listen_address`, `serving.page_http_listen_address`                                                                                             | Distinct ports (the examples use 4443 and 4444).                                                                                                                 |
| Gateway process             | spawned by the instance                                                                                                                                                                 | One gateway per instance. The core-to-gateway link is a socketpair, so it has no path to collide.                                                                |
| Identity                    | `serving.server_id`, `serving.server_name`                                                                                                                                              | Distinct `server_id`. The default is `orbbec-streamer@<hostname>`, the same for both instances on one host, so a client could not tell them apart.               |
| State                       | `calibration.camera_pose_path`, `calibration.placement_path`, `calibration.floor_path`, `encoding.depth.quantization_profile_path`, `run.sensor_config_path`, `run.stream_profile_path` | Distinct files. The defaults are relative to the working directory and shared by name (`floor_path` follows `camera_pose_path`, so it is distinct when that is). |
| Recording and logs          | `debug_recording.directory`                                                                                                                                                             | Distinct directory.                                                                                                                                              |
| Dev certificate hash        | `serving.dev_certificate_hash_path`                                                                                                                                                     | Distinct file. Each instance has its own certificate, so the browser pins one hash per server.                                                                   |
| Crash files                 | `serving.crash_directory`                                                                                                                                                               | Distinct directory.                                                                                                                                              |
| TensorRT engine cache       | `mask.rvm_engine_cache_dir`                                                                                                                                                             | May be shared. Builds take a lock file, and the same engine serves both.                                                                                         |

With one camera, set `sync.enabled: false` and give the camera the `primary` role, as the examples do. The two instances are not hardware-synchronised with each other; fusion across servers aligns by the clock sync of wire-format §14 and the capture timestamps, not by a trigger cable.

## Start [#start]

```sh
orbbec-streamer --live config/multi-server/rig-a.yaml
orbbec-streamer --live config/multi-server/rig-b.yaml
```

Calibrate and commit placement on each server separately (the setup lease is per server). A placement commit on one server changes nothing on the other. The client reads each server's `placementRevision` and `server.placement.updated`.

## Tested [#tested]

`gateway_serving_tests` runs two servers (each with its own controller, hub and fake gateway, one camera each) with one client. It checks that the two `serverId` values differ, that a placement commit on each (lease and `expectedRevision`) is acknowledged and announced by that server only, and that media reaches the client from both. A config test checks that the shipped examples share no port, path or identity.

`OrbbecDeviceCatalogUnitTests` uses a fake device list in which one camera is busy. It checks that listing opens no camera, that opening one serial touches only that camera, and that a busy camera you asked for fails with its serial number and port.

Not yet checked: two real rigs on one machine under load (needs the second rig).


# Rectification (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/rectification)



The wire contract (`protocol/wire-format.md` §7) says images are rectified on
the server, with no distortion coefficients on the wire. The server now does
this. With `streams.alignment: color_to_depth`, both encoded streams, depth and
colour, carry rectified images, so a client can unproject with the plain
pinhole intrinsics (`fx`, `fy`, `cx`, `cy`) it receives.

## What the server does [#what-the-server-does]

1. **Reads the lens data from the camera.** At start-up the server reads the
   depth and colour intrinsics, both distortion models (the model name and
   `k1`..`k6`, `p1`, `p2`) and the depth-to-colour extrinsic from the Orbbec
   SDK. It logs them once per camera:

   ```text
   Orbbec calibration: camera=orbbec:… depth: 640x576 fx=… fy=… cx=… cy=… distortion=brown-conrady-k6 k1=… k2=… k3=… k4=… k5=… k6=… p1=… p2=…
   Orbbec calibration: camera=orbbec:… colour: 1280x720 fx=… … distortion=…
   Orbbec calibration: camera=orbbec:… depth_to_colour (translation in millimetres): R=[…] t_mm=[…]
   ```

   The translation is in millimetres, unlike the metre-based poses elsewhere.
   Rectification itself does not use the colour lens or the extrinsic; the
   colour occlusion test of [Seam quality](./seam-quality) does.
2. **Builds one map per camera.** From the depth intrinsics and distortion it
   computes a remap table once, on the CPU, with OpenCV's
   `initUndistortRectifyMap`, and uploads it to the GPU. The rectified image
   keeps the same `fx`, `fy`, `cx`, `cy`, so nothing changes on the wire. A
   lens with no distortion needs no map and costs nothing per frame.
3. **Remaps every frame on the GPU**, first in the processing stage, before the
   depth filter, the masks and NVENC:
   * **Depth** uses nearest neighbour, so a value is never blended across a
     depth edge. Invalid depth (0) stays invalid, and a pixel whose source lies
     outside the camera image becomes invalid.
   * **Colour** uses bilinear interpolation, and only when colour is aligned
     to depth (`streams.alignment: color_to_depth`). Aligned colour sits on the
     depth pixel grid, so the depth lens model applies to it. A source outside
     the image becomes black. Native-size colour is not rectified.

The remap runs on the existing processing stream, takes its output buffers
from the buffer pool (no allocation per frame in steady state) and adds no
host synchronisation.

## When frames are not rectified [#when-frames-are-not-rectified]

Rectification never stops the server. When it cannot apply, the frames stream
as the camera made them, which is what earlier versions did, and the server
logs a warning once:

| Case                                                                                                        | What happens                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `streams.alignment: depth_to_color`                                                                         | Depth frames are colour-sized and the depth lens map does not fit them. No camera is rectified. This deviates from wire-format §7.  |
| `streams.alignment` disabled                                                                                | Colour is native, not on the depth grid. No camera is rectified, same deviation.                                                    |
| Depth lens model the server cannot rectify (modified or inverse Brown-Conrady, or a model a newer SDK adds) | That camera streams unrectified. The warning names the model; report the camera and its firmware version so the model can be added. |
| Depth distortion coefficients all zero                                                                      | An identity: nothing to do, no warning.                                                                                             |

Set `streams.alignment: color_to_depth` (the development config does) to get
rectified streams.

## Supported lens models [#supported-lens-models]

| SDK model                                  | Used by the server                  |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| none                                       | No remap                            |
| Brown-Conrady, Brown-Conrady k6            | Yes (OpenCV model)                  |
| Kannala-Brandt 4                           | Yes (OpenCV fisheye)                |
| Modified or inverse Brown-Conrady, unknown | No: that camera streams unrectified |

The Femto Bolt reports `brown-conrady-k6` for both depth and colour. Its depth
lens uses the large rational form (for example `k1` around 28 and `k4` around
28\); the map builds in a few milliseconds at start-up.

## Camera pose calibration uses the same images [#camera-pose-calibration-uses-the-same-images]

The calibration board is detected in rectified pixels: the engine remaps each
colour frame with the camera's map before detection, so the pose matches the
images the server streams. The corner overlay that the setup console draws is
in the same rectified pixels.

## Recalibrate after upgrading [#recalibrate-after-upgrading]

Camera pose files written by earlier versions were measured on images with lens
distortion in them. They still load and the server keeps using the saved poses,
but it logs one warning:

```text
calibrated before rectification - recalibration recommended
```

Run [camera pose calibration](./camera-calibration) again. Each pose write now
also writes `camera-pose.json.image-model` next to the file, a small sidecar
that records whether every camera was rectified (`rectified-v1`) or at least
one was not (`unrectified`, which logs its own warning). The marker is only on
disk; it is not on the wire.

The depth quantization profile is a histogram of depth values and does not
depend on lens geometry, so it needs no recalibration and has no marker.

### Downgrading [#downgrading]

The marker is a separate file, so `camera-pose.json` has exactly the keys older
servers require and they load it without a change. Nothing breaks on a
downgrade. If an older server then recalibrates, the sidecar's revision no
longer matches the pose, so a newer server reads that pose as "before
rectification" and warns.

## Recordings [#recordings]

The debug GPU-input recordings (`record_gpu_inputs`) are taken before
processing, so they hold the raw, unrectified frames. The GPU-output recordings
are the encoded streams and are rectified.

## GPU cost [#gpu-cost]

Measured with CUDA events on an RTX 4090, one camera at 640×576 (depth
nearest neighbour plus aligned colour bilinear), 500 frames after warm-up:

| Work per camera and frame | p50      | p99      | max      |
| ------------------------- | -------- | -------- | -------- |
| Depth and colour remap    | 0.009 ms | 0.009 ms | 0.021 ms |
| Depth remap alone         | 0.004 ms | 0.005 ms | 0.005 ms |

The map takes 2.9 MB of GPU memory per camera. The test is
`frame_rectifier_unit_tests`; it prints these numbers.


# Requirements (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/requirements)



The server runs on one Linux machine with an NVIDIA GPU and one or more Orbbec
cameras connected over USB. This page lists what that machine needs and gives a
command to check each item. The next page is [Install](./install).

## What you need [#what-you-need]

Only one configuration has been tested. Other versions may work, but nobody
has tried them.

| Component     | Tested version                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| OS            | Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64)                                                                                                                       |
| GPU           | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (compute capability 8.9)                                                                                                  |
| NVIDIA driver | 580.178.04                                                                                                                                        |
| CUDA toolkit  | 13.3 (`nvcc` V13.3.73), at `/usr/local/cuda`                                                                                                      |
| TensorRT      | 11.1.0.106 (`+cuda13.3` Debian packages)                                                                                                          |
| NVENC headers | `ffnvcodec` 12.1 (package `libffmpeg-nvenc-dev`)                                                                                                  |
| Orbbec SDK    | 2.8.7                                                                                                                                             |
| Cameras       | 2 × Orbbec Femto Bolt, firmware 1.1.2, hardware-synchronised                                                                                      |
| Compiler      | GCC 15.2 (`/usr/bin/gcc-15`, `/usr/bin/g++-15`)                                                                                                   |
| CMake / Ninja | CMake 4.1.2 and 4.2.3, Ninja 1.13.2                                                                                                               |
| Python        | 3.12 or newer, only to build the RVM engine                                                                                                       |
| Go            | Optional: 1.26 or newer runs `gateway_go_tests` (skipped without Go); the [WebTransport spike](./serving#try-the-webtransport-spike) needs 1.27.1 |

The first four checks below are about hardware and the OS, so run them before
you install anything. The software rows (CUDA, TensorRT, the Orbbec SDK, GCC)
come from [Install](./install); check them with step 5 afterwards.

## Check your machine [#check-your-machine]

### 1. Check the operating system [#1-check-the-operating-system]

```bash
lsb_release -d
```

You need Ubuntu 26.04. It is the only tested OS. The CMake presets
hard-code `/usr/bin/gcc-15`, `/usr/bin/g++-15` and `/usr/local/cuda`, which
the packages in [Install](./install) create.

### 2. Check the GPU and driver [#2-check-the-gpu-and-driver]

```bash
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,compute_cap --format=csv,noheader
```

Compare the output with these rules:

* **GPU generation.** The compute capability (the last number, which
  identifies the GPU generation) must be 7.5 (Turing) or higher. CUDA 13 does
  not support older GPUs. Use a GeForce, RTX or Quadro card. Compute GPUs
  without NVENC, such as the A100 and H100, do not work.
* **Driver.** The driver version must be 580 or newer, because CUDA 13.x needs
  driver branch 580. If `nvidia-smi` is missing, install a driver in
  [Install](./install#cuda-toolkit-and-driver).
* **Compute capability below 8.9.** The CMake presets compile the GPU code for
  compute capability 8.9 (RTX 40 series). They also include PTX (portable GPU
  code that the driver compiles at startup), so newer GPUs work unchanged. On
  a GPU below 8.9, such as an RTX 30 series card (8.6), the GPU code fails to
  run. You can still use it: follow
  [Build for a different GPU](./build#build-for-a-different-gpu) when you build.

The server also needs these NVENC features. You check them in step 6, after
the build:

* HEVC codec with the Main and Main10 profiles
* NV12 (8-bit) and YUV420 10-bit input surfaces
* 10-bit encoding
* the P1 preset (NVENC's fastest preset)

### 3. Check the cameras and their USB connection [#3-check-the-cameras-and-their-usb-connection]

With the cameras plugged in and powered, run:

```bash
lsusb | grep 2bc5
lsusb -t
```

`2bc5` is Orbbec's USB vendor ID. The first command must print one line per
camera. In the `lsusb -t` tree, each camera's interfaces must show `5000M`
(USB 3, 5 Gbit/s), not `480M` (USB 2).

About the cameras:

* **Model.** The only tested camera is the Orbbec Femto Bolt. The code talks to
  the Orbbec SDK, not to one camera model, but all cameras in one rig must be
  the same model.
* **Sync wiring.** With more than one camera, one camera is the `primary` and
  sends a hardware trigger to the others, the `secondary` cameras. You set the
  roles and delays later in the config file (`cameras[].role` and the `sync`
  block, see [Configuration](./configuration)). These pages do not describe
  the sync cabling. Wire the cameras as described in Orbbec's multi-camera
  synchronisation guide for your camera model.

### 4. Check the free disk space [#4-check-the-free-disk-space]

```bash
df -h ~
```

The build needs about 10 GB: one build directory with its vcpkg dependencies
takes about 5 GB, and the vcpkg binary cache in `~/.cache/vcpkg` takes about
another 4.5 GB. The CUDA toolkit and TensorRT packages need space on top of
that.

A display is optional. The live preview window opens only when `DISPLAY` or
`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set. Without a display, the server still runs and logs
that the preview is off.

### 5. Check the installed software [#5-check-the-installed-software]

Run this after you finish [Install](./install). On a fresh machine, these
commands fail until then.

```bash
/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc --version | tail -1
dpkg -l tensorrt-dev libnvinfer-bin orbbecsdk libffmpeg-nvenc-dev | grep ^ii
g++-15 --version | head -1
```

What each item is for:

* **CUDA toolkit** at `/usr/local/cuda`, with `nvcc` at
  `/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc`. It compiles the GPU code.
* **TensorRT** (`tensorrt-dev`) is required to build the server. Every server
  program links it, and CMake stops with an error if it cannot find the
  TensorRT headers and `libnvinfer`.
* **`trtexec`** (`libnvinfer-bin`) is optional. The server builds its RVM
  engine itself; only `scripts/setup_rvm.py` without `--skip-engine-build`
  uses `trtexec`, to prebuild the engines for the two RVM smoke tests.
* **Orbbec SDK** (`orbbecsdk`) talks to the cameras.
* **`ffnvcodec`** (`libffmpeg-nvenc-dev`) provides the NVENC API headers.
* **GCC 15** compiles the C++ code and is the host compiler for CUDA.

### 6. Check NVENC (after the build) [#6-check-nvenc-after-the-build]

After you [build the server](./build), run this from the `server/` folder:

```bash
./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --nvenc-test
```

It checks every NVENC feature listed in step 2 and names any that are missing.

## Expected result [#expected-result]

On the reference machine, steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 print:

```text
Description:	Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 580.178.04, 8.9
Bus 002 Device 002: ID 2bc5:066b Orbbec 3D Technology International, Inc Orbbec Femto Bolt 3D Camera
Bus 002 Device 003: ID 2bc5:066b Orbbec 3D Technology International, Inc Orbbec Femto Bolt 3D Camera
Build cuda_13.3.r13.3/compiler.38244171_0
ii  libffmpeg-nvenc-dev  12.1.14.0-1build1        …
ii  libnvinfer-bin       11.1.0.106-1+cuda13.3    …
ii  orbbecsdk            2.8.7                    …
ii  tensorrt-dev         11.1.0.106-1+cuda13.3    …
g++-15 (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0
```

Step 6 ends with `NVENC capability test passed` (full output in
[Build and test](./build#expected-result)).

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

| Symptom                                                                                                     | Cause and fix                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `nvidia-smi: command not found`, or it cannot talk to the driver                                            | No NVIDIA driver is loaded. Install one as described in [Install](./install#cuda-toolkit-and-driver), then reboot. |
| Compute capability is below 7.5                                                                             | CUDA 13 does not support this GPU. Use a newer GPU.                                                                |
| `--nvenc-test` fails with `NVENC does not support the required color/depth encoding pipeline. Missing: ...` | This GPU's NVENC cannot encode the 10-bit depth stream. Use a GPU that has these features.                         |
| `lsusb` shows no `2bc5` device                                                                              | Check the cable and the port, and use a USB 3 port. Some USB-C cables carry only USB 2 or only power.              |
| `lsusb -t` shows the camera at `480M`                                                                       | The camera is running at USB 2 speed. Move it to a USB 3 port or use a USB 3 cable.                                |


# Run the server (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/running)





`orbbec_streamer --live <config>` runs the full pipeline: capture from the configured Orbbec cameras, GPU processing, NVENC HEVC encoding and terminal telemetry. The other flags check the hardware and the SDKs. The live pipeline serves browsers only with `serving.enabled: true`: the control plane to every session, and each bundle's media streams to the sessions subscribed to it (see [Serve to browsers](./serving)). Encoded bundles also go to the debug recorder when it is on.

## Before you start [#before-you-start]

* **A built server**: `build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer`, or `build/dev-relwithdebinfo/orbbec_streamer` for latency measurements. See [Build and test](./build).
* **`server/` as working directory.** The config and the paths inside it are relative to it. Every command on this page runs from `server/`.
* **A config for your cameras**, adapted as below. All keys are in [Configuration](./configuration).

### Adapt the config to your rig [#adapt-the-config-to-your-rig]

As shipped, `config/dev/live.yaml` describes the development rig: two cameras by serial number (one `primary`, one `secondary`), hardware sync on, capture at 30 fps and stream at 15, `mask.backend: rvm` (its engine is not built by default), and GPU input and output recording to `debug/live`, which grows while the server runs.

1. Copy it into `config/local/`, which Git ignores:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p config/local
   cp config/dev/live.yaml config/local/live.yaml
   ```

2. Connect the cameras and note each device's `serial`:

   ```bash
   ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --orbbec-test
   ```

3. In `cameras`, add one entry per camera with its `serial_number`. With more than one camera, hardware sync is required: connect the sync cables, set `sync.enabled: true` and give exactly one camera `role: primary`. With a single camera set `sync.enabled: false`.

4. Choose the mask: keep `mask.backend: rvm` and point `mask.rvm_onnx_path` at the exported ONNX files ([Install](./install#rvm-segmentation-engine-optional)); the server builds the engine for your camera count on the first start, 3 to 4 minutes, while masks pass through ([details](./configuration#the-rvm-engine-cache)). Or set `mask.backend: fill_all`.

5. Decide on recording: set `debug_recording.record_gpu_inputs` and `record_gpu_outputs` to `false` to write only `setup.json`, or make sure `debug_recording.camera_ids` lists your camera `id`s and the disk has room.

The commands below use `config/dev/live.yaml`; substitute your copy.

## Check the hardware [#check-the-hardware]

Run these once on a new machine. Each prints its result and exits.

1. CUDA and NVENC:

   ```bash
   ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --cuda-test
   ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --nvenc-test
   ```

   `--cuda-test` ends with `CUDA smoke test OK`, `--nvenc-test` with `NVENC capability test passed`. `main10=true` and `encode_10bit=true` are required, because depth is 10-bit HEVC. Full output in [Build and test](./build#expected-result).

2. The Orbbec SDK and synchronised capture, with the cameras connected:

   ```bash
   ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --orbbec-test
   ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --orbbec-live-sync-test --config config/dev/live.yaml
   ```

   `--orbbec-test` lists every device (id, name, model, serial, firmware) and ends with `Orbbec provider smoke test OK`. `--orbbec-live-sync-test` opens the cameras as `--live` would, counts synchronised batches after a warm-up and ends with `PASS: production live configuration is synchronizing all cameras` (exit 0) or `FAIL: <reason>` (exit 1).

## Start the live pipeline [#start-the-live-pipeline]

1. Start the server:

   ```bash
   ./build/dev-debug/orbbec_streamer --live config/dev/live.yaml
   ```

2. Compare the start-up log with the [expected result](#expected-result).

3. After about 6 s the rate tables appear. `capture` runs at the capture rate, `upload` and `process` at the stream rate, `encode` at cameras × stream rate, all with `0` drops. See [Read the telemetry](./telemetry). With `mask.backend: rvm`, a `mask: ready, pass-through batches 0` line follows the table; `building` or `failed` means masks pass every pixel ([details](./configuration#the-rvm-engine-cache)).

On an interactive terminal the tables are redrawn in place. To keep every table in a log file instead:

```bash
ORBBEC_STREAMER_STATUS_MODE=log ./build/dev-relwithdebinfo/orbbec_streamer --live config/dev/live.yaml 2>&1 | tee live.log
```

## Expected result [#expected-result]

A healthy start with two synchronised cameras, capture 30 / stream 15, `mask.backend: fill_all` and no display (abridged):

```text
[info] depth quantization profile not found at 'config/dev/depth-quantization.json'; using linear 10-bit mapping over [500,5000] mm
[info] live config: cameras=2 wait_timeout_ms=5000 preview=true
[info] live streams: depth=640x576@30 depth_u16 color=1280x720@30 rgb8
[info] live encoding: enabled=true mode=concatenated_batch gpu=0 queue=2 gop=60 depth_quantization=linear ...
[info] active camera: config_id=cam0 serial=CL8K0000000A name='Orbbec Femto Bolt'
[info] active camera: config_id=cam1 serial=CL8K0000000B name='Orbbec Femto Bolt'
[info] live selected 2 active camera(s), neglected 0 camera(s)
[info] opened camera: serial=CL8K0000000A firmware='1.1.2'
[info] opened camera: serial=CL8K0000000B firmware='1.1.2'
[info] live queues: capacity=2 per GPU stage (drop oldest), encode=2, upload slots=41
[info] frame rate: capture 30 fps, stream 15 fps (1 of every 2 captured batches goes on)
Configured Orbbec sync: camera=orbbec:CL8K0000000A mode=4 depth_delay_us=0 ... global_timestamp=enabled
Configured Orbbec sync: camera=orbbec:CL8K0000000B mode=8 depth_delay_us=160 ... global_timestamp=enabled
Enabled Orbbec device clock synchronization after stream startup: interval_ms=0 (0: once)
[info] wrote live setup metadata: debug/live/setup.json
[info] setup at startup: phase=NEEDS_SETUP readiness=needs-setup camera_pose_calibration=missing (revision 0: ...) streaming=stopped metadata_revision=1
[info] live pipeline started: cameras=2 streams=2 alignment_mode=1 mask_backend=fill_all ...
[warning] no DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY is available; disabling the live preview window
```

What to check:

* `neglected 0 camera(s)`: every configured camera was found.
* One `Configured Orbbec sync` line per camera: `mode=4` is the primary, `mode=8` a secondary.
* `live pipeline started`: capture, processing and encoding run.
* `setup at startup: ... needs-setup`: no camera-pose calibration saved yet; the pipeline runs anyway. See [Camera pose calibration](./camera-calibration).

With `run.preview: true` and a display, a preview window opens at the first processed frame. It shows every camera, one row each: aligned colour, filtered depth as a colour map, and the mask (all white with `fill_all`). Each panel is labelled with the camera id. The images are the rectified ones the encoder gets. Colour is black where the camera measured no depth. Press `q` or `Esc` in it to stop the server. The preview runs on its own thread and never slows the pipeline.

<img alt="Live preview window: aligned colour, filtered depth and mask panels of the first camera (the window shows one such row per camera)" src="__img0" />

## Debug recording output [#debug-recording-output]

With `record_gpu_inputs` or `record_gpu_outputs` on, files go to `debug_recording.directory` (default `debug/live`) and the server prints a `DEBUG RECORDING` table with every path:

```text
debug/live/
  setup.json                        always written, even with recording off
  manifest.json                     record_gpu_outputs (raw .hevc): what the recording holds
  cam0/gpu-input-color.mkv          record_gpu_inputs: colour entering the GPU (FFV1)
  cam0/gpu-input-depth.mkv          record_gpu_inputs: depth entering the GPU (FFV1, 16-bit)
  cam0/gpu-output-layout.json       tile layout and depth packing
  cam0/gpu-output-color.hevc        record_gpu_outputs: raw HEVC (Annex B), per_camera
  cam0/gpu-output-depth.hevc
  multicam/                         the same files, in concatenated_batch mode
    gpu-output-layout.json
    gpu-output-color.hevc
    gpu-output-depth.hevc
    gpu-output-color.mkv            locally_decode_gpu_outputs: decoded colour (FFV1)
    gpu-output-depth.mkv            decoded 10-bit depth codes (FFV1)
    gpu-output-depth-inferno.mkv    depth as a colour map, 500-3000 mm
```

* FFV1 is lossless, so inputs hold the exact frames. Annex B is the plain HEVC byte stream.
* In `per_camera` mode encoded output goes to each camera's folder (`cam0/gpu-output-*`); in `concatenated_batch` mode it goes to `multicam/`.
* Folder names are the camera `id`s. A camera `id` that is not a valid folder name (empty, `.` or `..`, or containing `/` or `\`, or longer than 128 characters or 255 bytes) has no encoded output recorded; the server logs the reason at start. Its `record_gpu_inputs` files, if enabled, are still written, under a folder name with the invalid characters replaced by `_`.
* Recordings run at the stream rate.
* Recordings are closed at shutdown; stop the server with a signal, never `kill -9`.

### The recording manifest [#the-recording-manifest]

`manifest.json` lets a reader play the raw `.hevc` files without the server. It follows protocol change 0038 in the revision agreed on the branch `client/cr-0038-recording-manifest` (status: proposed; the text on `main` is an older draft, so the format can still change). It is written with the raw `.hevc` output only, not with `locally_decode_gpu_outputs`, and only when the client-facing setup exists (`streams.alignment: color_to_depth`). It holds, as of the recording start:

* server identity (`serverId`, `serverName`), `streamLayout` (`per-camera` or `concatenated`) and `frameRate` (the stream rate);
* `startCaptureTimeUs`, the capture time of frame set 0 (the first frame set the recorder was offered) in server monotonic microseconds;
* `cameras` (depth intrinsics and poses), `quantization` (including the 1024-entry LUT), `placement`, `calibrationRevision` and `metadataRevision`, in the same form as the live messages;
* `bundles`: for each bundle the camera ids, tiles, the relative paths of its colour and depth files, and its `segments`;
* `recording`: `state` and `droppedFrameSets`.

**Frame set index.** The recorder numbers the frame sets it is offered 0, 1, 2, and so on, before its queue, one per batch. A frame set the queue drops still uses its number; frame sets that were never streamed (capture-rate decimation) do not. The number is the same in every bundle, so it is how a reader lines the bundles up. It is not derived from timestamps.

**Segments.** Each bundle writes its colour and depth files independently. A file starts at the bundle's first frame set whose colour and depth are both IDR, and a `segment` records `firstFrameSetIndex` and, once closed, `accessUnits`. After a gap in a bundle (a dropped frame set, or a frame set without that bundle) the bundle discards frame sets until its own next IDR and starts a new segment. It does not wait for the other bundles, and the server never forces a keyframe for the recording. The frame sets a bundle discarded are the holes between its segments.

**Lifecycle.** The server writes the manifest when the recording starts, `in-progress`, with every bundle listed and empty `segments`, so a crash still leaves a manifest. It rewrites it each time a bundle starts a segment (the previous segment gets its `accessUnits`, the new one is open), before the new segment's first access unit is appended, so access units after a gap are never counted in the previous segment. At a clean shutdown it writes `complete`, with every segment closed, after flushing the `.hevc` files to disk. Each write goes to a temporary file in the same folder, is flushed and renamed over `manifest.json`, and the folder is flushed too, so a reader never sees half a manifest. A bundle that never reached an IDR has nothing to play: at a clean shutdown the server leaves it out of the final manifest, deletes its empty files and logs it. If no bundle reached an IDR, or the recorder failed, the manifest stays `in-progress`.

Because a recording can only start at an IDR, `debug_recording.record_gpu_outputs` is refused with `encoding.gop_length: 0`. A bundle waits up to one `gop_length` for its next IDR; after two GOPs without one the log warns (at most once per two GOPs and bundle).

A recording that starts before the setup state exists waits for it; those frame sets are not recorded. If the setup state never appears, no `manifest.json` is written and the log says so. A `manifest.json` left by an earlier run is removed when the server starts recording. A camera `id` is also refused when `<id>/gpu-output-color.hevc` is longer than 255 bytes; the other cameras still record.

## Stop the server [#stop-the-server]

1. Press `Ctrl+C`, or from another terminal:

   ```bash
   pkill -TERM -f 'orbbec_streamer --live'
   ```

2. Within a few seconds the server stops capture, upload, processing and encoding in that order, closes the recordings and prints the session summary and totals.

Expected last line: `[info] live stop requested; pipeline stopped cleanly`.

If a worker thread or a camera fails, the cameras stop the same way. Without a setup plane (`streams.alignment` other than `color_to_depth`) the server then logs `orbbec-streamer failed: <reason>` and exits with code 1. With one, it stays up with `capture` set to `failed` and the reason in the log and in `capture.message` (see [Cameras closed and capture start](./serving#cameras-closed-and-capture-start)); it does not retry by itself. A server started with `serving.start_capture_on_launch: false` keeps the cameras closed until a client asks for them, so no camera lines appear in the log before that. `Ctrl+C` while it still waits for cameras ends it at once with `live stop requested while waiting for cameras; nothing started`.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

The Orbbec SDK logs to `Log/OrbbecSDK.log.txt` in the working directory; look there first for camera errors.

| Symptom                                                                                                                                                         | Cause and fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Request failed, device response with unknown error! propertyId: 1038` after the first `Configured Orbbec sync` line                                            | A camera rejected the multi-device sync settings and is stuck, often after a `kill -9` during streaming. Restarting the server does not help; power-cycle every camera (disconnect power and USB, wait, reconnect).                                                                                                                                    |
| `Orbbec synchronization role readback mismatch for camera <id>`                                                                                                 | The camera didn't accept its role. Check the sync cable and `cameras[].role`, then power-cycle.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `neglecting missing camera: config_id=... serial='...'`                                                                                                         | Not found within `run.camera_wait_timeout_ms`. Check USB and the serial with `--orbbec-test`. The server continues without it, even with `required: true`.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `No configured cameras are active; live mode cannot continue`                                                                                                   | No configured camera found. Same checks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `camera capture stopped: [<id>: Orbbec capture error: ...]`                                                                                                     | A camera failed or was unplugged; the server stops rather than run with cameras missing. Check USB and power, then restart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `camera capture stopped: [<id>: no frame set for N ms (dropped before batching: I invalid timestamp, B backwards timestamp, J timestamp jump, A align failed)]` | No usable frame set for more than 5 s without an error. All counts 0: the camera delivered nothing (firmware hang, USB fault); check USB and power, power-cycle if it repeats. A high count: frames arrive but are dropped; `invalid timestamp` means no global timestamps (restart, then power-cycle), `align failed` points at the alignment filter. |
| `camera capture stopped: [no batch for N ms: the cameras' frame sets no longer match within the timestamp tolerance ...]`                                       | Every camera delivers but no batch formed for 5 s (10 s before the first): the timestamps disagree more than the batcher can follow. Check the sync cable and roles, restart; power-cycle if it persists.                                                                                                                                              |
| `camera capture stopped: [frame sets of different trigger slots matched by timestamp ...]`                                                                      | The frame counters disagree and the timestamps are too far apart to tell which frames belong together. The batch was not sent. A lost trigger alone is re-learned and does not stop the server. Check the sync cable and roles, then restart.                                                                                                          |
| `frame batcher dropped N frame set(s) without a match from every camera`                                                                                        | At 15 fps capture, about one drop per camera every 20 to 30 s is normal (the colour sensor skips a frame every 399). At 30 fps, drops after start-up point to sync or timestamps: check the sync cable and roles. See [Capture and synchronisation](./how-it-works/capture-and-sync#frame-batching).                                                   |
| `processing (bilateral filter at depth WxH): Resolved bilateral radius exceeds maximum_radius_pixels`                                                           | Lower `processing.bilateral_radius_ratio` or raise `bilateral_maximum_radius_pixels`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Orbbec global timestamps are required ... not supported by camera`                                                                                             | Update the camera firmware.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--cuda-test` prints `CUDA error: ...`                                                                                                                          | No usable CUDA device or driver; check `nvidia-smi`. It still exits 0, so read its output.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `cudaMalloc failed: ...` or another CUDA error                                                                                                                  | Check the driver and free GPU memory with `nvidia-smi`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `NvEncOpenEncodeSessionEx failed with NVENC status 10`                                                                                                          | No NVENC session available (`NV_ENC_ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`, also returned at the driver's session limit). The server opens 2 sessions in `concatenated_batch`, 2 per camera in `per_camera`. Stop other encoders and check `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=encoder.stats.sessionCount --format=csv`.                                                               |
| `RVM engine` progress lines, and masks that keep everything                                                                                                     | The engine is building on first start (3 to 4 minutes). The `LIVE PIPELINE` table shows `mask: building, pass-through batches <n>`; wait for `built TensorRT engine` and `segmentation ready`. `mask: failed` means the build or load failed: read the `[error]` line.                                                                                 |
| `ONNX model not found: ...`                                                                                                                                     | `mask.rvm_onnx_path` does not point at an exported model. Export it with `scripts/setup_rvm.py --skip-engine-build` or use `fill_all`. The server keeps running with all-foreground masks; look for this `[error]` line and `mask: failed` in the stats.                                                                                               |
| `segmentation unavailable: ... Cannot open TensorRT engine: ...`                                                                                                | Only with the `mask.rvm_engine_path` override and a missing, incompatible or wrong-batch engine (a `live.yaml` kept from an older install). The server keeps running with all-foreground masks and `mask: failed` in the tables; remove `rvm_engine_path` and set `rvm_onnx_path` and `rvm_engine_cache_dir`, or use `fill_all`, then restart.         |
| `--calibrate-camera-pose requires streams.alignment: color_to_depth`                                                                                            | Set that alignment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `setup state not built: client-facing setup requires streams.alignment=color_to_depth`                                                                          | Warning only: the pipeline runs without a setup state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `the preview window did not close within 2 s ...; exiting without waiting for it`                                                                               | The display server stopped answering. The server has already stopped everything and written its summary. Check `DISPLAY` or set `run.preview: false`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `no DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY is available; disabling the live preview window`                                                                                 | Warning only. Set `run.preview: false` to silence it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `upload queue full: ...`, `processing queue full: ...`, `encode queue full: ...`                                                                                | A stage fell behind and its queue dropped the oldest batch. See [Read the telemetry](./telemetry#troubleshooting).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Failed to open live config: <path>`                                                                                                                            | Run from `server/` or pass an absolute path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

## Command-line reference [#command-line-reference]

| Flag                                     | Argument    | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--live`                                 | config file | Runs the live pipeline until stopped.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--calibrate-camera-pose`                | none        | With `--live`: runs a camera-pose calibration from the local console and saves it.                                                                                                          |
| `--print-charuco-board`                  | PNG path    | Writes the calibration board as a 300 dpi PNG and exits. Uses the board from `--live <config>` if given. Not combinable with `--calibrate-camera-pose`.                                     |
| `--cuda-test`                            | none        | Prints the CUDA devices and launches a trivial kernel without checking the launch, so it prints `CUDA smoke test OK` even for a wrong GPU architecture; use `ctest -L unit` to detect that. |
| `--nvenc-test`                           | none        | Checks the NVENC HEVC features the server needs.                                                                                                                                            |
| `--compression-test`, `--websocket-test` | none        | Placeholders that print `... smoke test OK` and test nothing.                                                                                                                               |
| `--orbbec-test`                          | none        | Lists the connected Orbbec devices.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--orbbec-capture-test`                  | none        | Captures from all connected cameras through GPU upload and prints frame rates.                                                                                                              |
| `--orbbec-live-sync-test`                | none        | Checks synchronised capture with a live config.                                                                                                                                             |
| `--config`                               | config file | Config for `--orbbec-live-sync-test` only. Default `config/dev/live.yaml`.                                                                                                                  |
| `--warmup-s`, `--duration-s`             | seconds     | Warm-up (`5`) and measurement time (`10`) for `--orbbec-live-sync-test`.                                                                                                                    |
| `--minimum-rate-ratio`                   | ratio       | Pass threshold: measured batch rate / configured depth fps. Default `0.9`.                                                                                                                  |
| `-h`, `--help`                           | none        | Prints the flags.                                                                                                                                                                           |

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` run-time error (`orbbec-streamer failed: <reason>`), `2` invalid flag combination, or a CLI11 parse error code (for example `109` for an unknown flag).


# Seam quality (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/seam-quality)



Colour is aligned to depth by the Orbbec SDK (`streams.alignment:
color_to_depth`). At a silhouette that alignment can put the colour of the
person onto the depth of the wall behind them. A client then shows a
head-coloured patch lying flat on the wall, or a thin curtain of points in the
air between the head and the wall. This page describes the three GPU passes
that remove those pixels, the configuration keys, and how to check the effect
on a camera. Nothing on the wire changes: the passes only turn more depth
pixels into code 0, which already means "invalid" (wire format §8).

## Why it happens [#why-it-happens]

* **Parallax.** The colour sensor sits about 3 cm from the depth sensor. A
  wall pixel right beside the head is seen by the depth sensor but hidden from
  the colour sensor, because the head is in front of it. The SDK's alignment
  looks the colour up for every depth pixel and does not test for this, so the
  wall pixel gets the colour of the head. The band is one-sided, on the side of
  the head away from the colour sensor. Its width in depth pixels is
  `fx × baseline × (1 / z_near − 1 / z_far)`: about 8 pixels for a person at
  1.2 m in front of a wall at 3 m, and shrinking as the person moves back.
* **Mixed pixels.** The depth of a pixel on a silhouette is often a mixture of
  the two surfaces ("flying pixel"), or missing. The bilateral filter used to
  average across the jump and to fill missing depth from the neighbours, which
  made more mixtures.
* **Mask overreach.** The soft matte can extend a few pixels past the true
  silhouette, onto the wall.

## What the server does [#what-the-server-does]

All three passes run on the processing stream, per camera, after
[rectification](./rectification) and the mask. The source depth buffer is never
modified (calibration and the recorders read it). They apply with
`processing.depth_filter_backend: bilateral_cuda`; `identity_copy` stays a pure
copy so the filter and mapping can be compared with it.

1. **Colour occlusion test.** Every valid depth pixel is projected into the
   colour image (using the colour intrinsics, lens model and the
   depth-to-colour extrinsic read from the camera) and its depth in the colour
   frame is kept in a z-buffer. A depth pixel that is more than a tolerance
   behind the nearest surface at its colour pixel, or at a neighbouring cell
   (to absorb the small mismatch between this projection and the SDK's), is
   invalid. This needs `streams.alignment: color_to_depth` and a usable colour
   calibration; a camera without one only loses this pass, with a warning.
2. **Flying pixels and silhouette band.**
   * A pixel whose depth differs from a valid neighbour by more than
     `max(flying_pixel_jump_mm, flying_pixel_jump_ratio × the nearer depth)` is
     invalid. A smooth surface is far below that: at 1.5 m one pixel is about
     3 mm.
   * Mask erosion happens only at depth jumps: a masked pixel close to the mask
     edge that lies behind a nearer masked surface is invalid, so overreach onto
     the wall goes, while a silhouette where the depths agree (feet on the
     floor, a hand on the body) keeps every pixel. One more pixel of foreground
     is dropped where the mask edge is itself a depth jump.
3. **Bilateral filter.** Flagged pixels are invalid and never contribute to a
   neighbour. A depth range term lowers the weight of neighbours at another
   depth: it is flat within `s = max(bilateral_depth_sigma_mm,
   bilateral_depth_sigma_ratio × depth)` (sensor noise is smoothed as before)
   and Gaussian beyond it. A neighbour above the jump threshold never
   contributes. A pixel without depth stays invalid
   (`bilateral_fill_holes: false`); the filter does not invent depth.

Pixels removed this way are holes. With two cameras the other camera usually
fills them in the fused cloud; where it cannot, the hole is the price of not
showing the wrong colour.

## Configuration [#configuration]

All keys are in the `processing` section, optional, and on by default. They
are checked when the file is loaded; a value out of range, negative or not a
finite number stops start-up with the key's name.

| Key                            | Type    | Default | Range             | Effect                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------ | ------- | ------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seam_filter_enabled`          | bool    | `true`  |                   | Master switch for the occlusion test and the flying-pixel and silhouette passes. The filter's own range term and hole policy (below) stay as set. |
| `occlusion_test_enabled`       | bool    | `true`  |                   | The colour occlusion test alone. Active with `color_to_depth` only; with another alignment it is off, with one warning.                           |
| `occlusion_tolerance_mm`       | float   | `20`    | ≥ 0               | A pixel is occluded when it is further than the nearest surface by more than `max(this, ratio × depth)`.                                          |
| `occlusion_tolerance_ratio`    | float   | `0.02`  | ≥ 0               | Relative part of the tolerance.                                                                                                                   |
| `occlusion_zbuffer_downsample` | integer | `2`     | 1–4               | The z-buffer has the colour image size divided by this. 2 closes the gaps between projected depth pixels.                                         |
| `occlusion_neighbourhood_px`   | integer | `1`     | 0–2               | Cells around the pixel's own that are searched for a nearer surface.                                                                              |
| `flying_pixel_radius_px`       | integer | `1`     | 0–3               | Window radius for the flying-pixel test. 0 turns it off.                                                                                          |
| `flying_pixel_jump_mm`         | float   | `30`    | ≥ 0               | Fixed part of the jump threshold.                                                                                                                 |
| `flying_pixel_jump_ratio`      | float   | `0.03`  | ≥ 0               | Relative part of the jump threshold. Not both zero while the radius is above 0.                                                                   |
| `seam_erode_px`                | integer | `2`     | 0–4               | A masked pixel this close to the mask edge is removed when it lies behind a nearer surface. 0 turns it off.                                       |
| `seam_search_px`               | integer | `4`     | `seam_erode_px`–8 | How far to look for the nearer surface.                                                                                                           |
| `seam_foreground_erode_px`     | integer | `1`     | 0–2               | Foreground pixels removed where the mask edge is a depth jump.                                                                                    |
| `bilateral_depth_sigma_mm`     | float   | `10`    | ≥ 0               | Fixed part of the range sigma. Both sigmas 0 turns the range term off.                                                                            |
| `bilateral_depth_sigma_ratio`  | float   | `0.01`  | ≥ 0               | Relative part of the range sigma.                                                                                                                 |
| `bilateral_fill_holes`         | bool    | `false` |                   | `true` brings back the old behaviour: a pixel without depth takes its neighbours' mean.                                                           |
| `mask_foreground_threshold`    | integer | `128`   | 0–255             | Foreground when the mask is at least this. Used by the filter, by the passes above and by the depth calibration.                                  |

`bilateral_mask_threshold` is deprecated. It was parsed but never applied
before 0.1.6: the filter always used 128, whatever the file said (the earlier
example configurations said 32). The working setting is the new
`mask_foreground_threshold`. The old key is still read and range-checked
(0–255) but ignored, and when it is present the server logs one warning at
start-up. If both are present, `mask_foreground_threshold` is used. An existing
configuration therefore keeps the effective 128 with no edit; remove the old
key when convenient. Set `mask_foreground_threshold` below 128 only if you want
a wider foreground mask, which also widens the overreach the passes have to
remove.

To get the filter as it was before these passes, set `seam_filter_enabled:
false`, `bilateral_depth_sigma_mm: 0`, `bilateral_depth_sigma_ratio: 0` and
`bilateral_fill_holes: true`.

## Cost [#cost]

Measured on the RTX 4090 with the `dev-relwithdebinfo` build, at the largest
depth size (1024 × 1024), 200 launches, while other work shared the GPU
(busy machine, treat as an upper bound):

| Per camera                                                                | p50      | p99            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------- |
| Occlusion test and flying-pixel/silhouette passes (including both clears) | 0.044 ms | 0.054–0.060 ms |
| Bilateral filter, new                                                     | 0.089 ms | 0.092–0.097 ms |
| Bilateral filter, before                                                  | 0.074 ms | 0.077–0.081 ms |
| Added by the change                                                       | 0.06 ms  |                |

At 640 × 576 it is proportionally smaller. No host synchronisation and no
allocation per frame is added: the flag image and the z-buffer are allocated
once and reused.

## Check it on a real camera [#check-it-on-a-real-camera]

The check records for about 20 s from one camera, no board needed, and prints
the numbers before and after. Stop the service first (one process owns the
cameras), put a person in front of a wall or some furniture with straight
edges in view, and run, from `server/`:

```bash
build/dev-relwithdebinfo/orbbec_streamer_seam_quality_check --config config/dev/live.yaml --seconds 20 --output seam-quality.json
```

It reports, for the first camera of the configuration (`--camera <id>` picks
another):

* **Flying (mixed) depth pixels per frame**, in the rectified source depth,
  after the filter as it was before (BEFORE) and after the passes and the new
  filter (AFTER). A mixed pixel differs from both neighbours of an opposite
  pair by more than the jump threshold; a clean step edge is not counted.
* **Valid depth pixels per frame** after each filter, and the share of the
  valid depth the occlusion test and the flying-pixel pass removed.
* **Straightness of long edges** (at least 120 px) in the raw and in the
  rectified colour image: the RMS distance of the edge pixels to their fitted
  line, median and 90th percentile. After rectification the long edges of a
  door frame or a table should be straight to a fraction of a pixel.

The mask in this check is "everything is foreground" (no RVM), so it measures
the occlusion test and the flying-pixel pass; the silhouette band needs a mask
and is covered by the unit tests. The check does not write to the
configuration or the pose files.

For a visual comparison on the whole pipeline, run the same scene four times
with the debug recording on, changing only `mask.backend` (`fill_all`, `rvm`)
and `processing.depth_filter_backend` (`identity_copy`, `bilateral_cuda`), and
look at the wall beside the head in each. `fill_all` with `identity_copy` shows
the alignment alone; `rvm` with `bilateral_cuda` is the production setting.

## Limits [#limits]

* The projection into the colour image uses the lens model that the camera
  reports. Brown-Conrady, its six-coefficient form and Kannala-Brandt are
  handled; the camera's "modified Brown-Conrady" model is treated as the
  six-coefficient form, and an unknown or inverse model as a pinhole. This
  has not been compared with the SDK's own alignment on a camera; the
  neighbourhood and the tolerance cover a small mismatch, not a wrong model.
* Colour that falls outside the colour sensor's field of view is not flagged.
* The passes remove wrong pixels; they do not recover colour for them. A
  client that wants no holes needs the second camera's view of the same place.
* Colour mixing from 4:2:0 chroma subsampling and HEVC ringing at an edge
  happens after these passes and is not addressed here.


# Serve to browsers (https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/serving)



Browsers will connect over WebTransport, a browser API for low-latency streams over HTTP/3 and QUIC, always encrypted with TLS. The session shape (one control stream, one stream per media channel) is fixed by `protocol/wire-format.md` §1; this page does not restate the contract.

## Status [#status]

**Off by default.** With `serving.enabled: true` (see [Configuration](./configuration#serving)), `--live` starts the Go WebTransport gateway, supervises it and serves every browser session: the control stream (`client.hello`, snapshots, pings, the setup lease and calibration commands) and, since CR 0009 is accepted, the media streams of the bundles the session subscribed to.

**Media flows on subscribe.** A session receives nothing until it subscribes to a bundle, by naming it in `preferredBundleIds` of `client.hello` or by sending `client.subscribe`. The server then opens that bundle's colour and depth streams at the first keyframe it can give the session (it asks the encoder for one when the session joins). `client.unsubscribe` finishes both streams: an `endOfStream` record (flags `0x04`, no payload), then FIN. Subscribing again opens new streams.

**A slow client costs the others few keyframes.** When a session falls behind and needs a keyframe to recover, the server asks the encoder for one, at most once per 2 s across all sessions. A session that needs it again soon doubles its own wait (up to 60 s) and meanwhile recovers at the next regular keyframe or when its wait is over and it asks again, so one client that never reads cannot make every viewer decode an extra keyframe every two seconds. A session that then stays out of trouble for 30 s starts from 2 s again. A new subscriber still gets its keyframe at once. Recovery needs regular keyframes as a fallback, so `serving.enabled` is refused with `encoding.gop_length: 0`.

**Telemetry.** Every 10 s the server logs, per bundle with subscribers: `sessions`, `queued_max` and `queued_total` (frame sets waiting in the per-session queues), `rotation_pause`, `stale_generation` and `no_generation` (records dropped because of a revision change), `forced_keyframes`, `suppressed` and `rotated`. All counters are cumulative.

**How media streams end.** The same line ends with `closes{eos_fin=.. fin_only=.. stop_sending=.. reset=.. write_error=.. session_closed=..}`, cumulative counters of how each colour or depth stream ended. `eos_fin` is an `endOfStream` record followed by FIN (an unsubscribe, or the old stream of a revision rotation). `fin_only` is FIN alone, when no record was accepted on the stream (CR 0040 A). `stop_sending` is the browser cancelling one stream; the session lives on and the channel reopens at the next keyframe. `write_error` and `session_closed` are streams that died with their session, with no `endOfStream` record: the first when the gateway ended the session after a stream I/O failure (every stream of that session counts, not only the one that failed), the second for any other session end (client left, idle timeout, core close, gateway loss, shutdown). `reset` is reserved for a stream the server itself aborts and stays 0 today. Each close also logs one debug line (visible with debug logging only, so a reconnect storm cannot flood the log), `serving: media <bundle>: stream closed session=<id>:<epoch> channel=<color|depth> stream=<id> reason=<reason>`, once per stream and never per frame.
